definition_zh: 推断；演绎；由……推出；推导
definition_en: to reach a conclusion by reasoning from evidence or from general principles
core_image: 一串脚印从泥地延伸到矮墙下，看的人顺着痕迹一步步把结论领出来
scene: 侦探看到窗台上的灰被擦去一半，便由这条痕迹推出有人从窗子进出。From the half-wiped dust the detective deduced that someone had used the window.
sceneCN: 这里指依据现场痕迹推出事实（第 6 个义项：由实物线索推断出事实）；句意：侦探从被擦去一半的灰尘推断有人用过那扇窗。

senses.title: To reach a conclusion by reasoning
senses.definition: to work out a conclusion from evidence rather than from direct observation
senses.definitionCN: 由证据而非直接观察得出一个结论
senses.example: From the marks on the wall they deduced that the water had once been higher.
senses.exampleCN: 他们从墙上的痕迹推断出水位曾经更高。
senses.why: The Latin verb means to lead down, so the mind is led from the evidence down to the conclusion.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁动词意为向下引领，心智被从证据一路领到结论。

senses.title: To derive a case from premises (logic)
senses.titleCN: 在逻辑上由前提出发推出
senses.definition: in logic, to derive a particular statement from general premises by a valid step
senses.definitionCN: 在逻辑中，由一般前提出发经有效步骤推出具体陈述
senses.example: From the two premises the class deduced that no exception could exist.
senses.exampleCN: 由这两个前提，全班推出不可能存在例外。
senses.why: Logic made the downward leading a formal procedure with rules that fix what may follow.
senses.whyCN: 逻辑学把这种向下引领变成有规则约束的正式程序，规定什么可以推出。

senses.title: To trace something to its source (formal)
senses.definition: in formal or older usage, to trace a fact or a word back to its origin
senses.definitionCN: 在正式或较早用法中，把某个事实或词语追溯到其来源
senses.example: The custom may be deduced from an older harvest rite.
senses.exampleCN: 这一习俗也许可以追溯到一种更古老的收获仪式。
senses.why: Led down also means followed back along a chain, which is how origins are recovered.
senses.whyCN: 向下引领也意味着沿链条反推，追溯来源正是这样完成的。

senses.title: To work out a meaning from context
senses.definition: to infer the sense of a word or a passage from the surrounding text
senses.definitionCN: 由上下文推断词或段落的意思
senses.example: Readers deduce the meaning of an unfamiliar word from the sentence around it.
senses.exampleCN: 读者从周围的句子推断出生词的意思。
senses.why: Language gives partial evidence, and the mind fills the rest by the same leading-down path.
senses.whyCN: 语言提供部分证据，心智沿同一条向下引领的路径把其余部分补上。

senses.title: To derive a rule from data
senses.definition: to extract a general rule or pattern from a set of observations
senses.definitionCN: 从一组观察中抽出一条一般规律或模式
senses.example: The analysts deduced a seasonal pattern from three years of sales.
senses.exampleCN: 分析师从三年的销售数据推出一个季节性规律。
senses.why: Data is the premise and the rule is the conclusion, so the verb names the path between them.
senses.whyCN: 数据是前提，规律是结论，这个动词命名的是两者之间的路径。

senses.title: To infer facts from physical clues
senses.definition: to reconstruct what happened from traces left in the physical world
senses.definitionCN: 根据物质世界留下的痕迹重建事情经过
senses.example: From the half-wiped dust the detective deduced that someone had used the window.
senses.exampleCN: 侦探从被擦去一半的灰尘推断有人用过那扇窗。
senses.why: Clues are premises written in matter, and the detective's work is the old verb in its most dramatic form.
senses.whyCN: 线索是用物质写成的前提，侦探的工作就是这个古老动词最戏剧化的形态。

senses.title: To derive a formula or result (mathematics)
senses.definition: in mathematics, to obtain a result by a sequence of valid steps
senses.definitionCN: 在数学中，通过一系列有效步骤得到结果
senses.example: The students deduced the area formula from the rectangle.
senses.exampleCN: 学生们由矩形面积推出了那个面积公式。
senses.why: Mathematics is the home of the downward step, where each line must follow from the one before.
senses.whyCN: 数学是这种向下推步的主场，每一行都必须由前一行推出。

senses.title: To work out consequences of a theory
senses.definition: to set out what must follow if a theory or an assumption is accepted
senses.definitionCN: 说明若接受某个理论或假设，必然会出现什么
senses.example: If the model is right, we can deduce where the particles should appear.
senses.exampleCN: 如果模型正确，我们就能推知粒子应当出现在哪里。
senses.why: A theory is judged by its consequences, and drawing them out is the everyday work of the verb.
senses.whyCN: 理论靠其后果受检验，把后果推出来正是这个动词的日常工作。

intro.en: Deduce comes from a Latin verb meaning to lead down or to draw off, built from a prefix of downward movement and the verb for leading. English took it in the sixteenth century, and logic fixed the sense of deriving a conclusion.
intro.cn: 本词出自一个表示向下引领或引出的拉丁动词，由表示向下的前缀与表示引领的动词构成。英语在十六世纪借入，逻辑学固定了「推出结论」的含义。

items.en: Ducere meant to lead or to draw, and it stands behind many English words of conducting and producing.
items.cn: 这个拉丁动词意为引领、牵引，英语中许多表示引导与产出的词都出自它。

items.en: The prefix meant down or away, so the compound pictured a movement downward along a path.
items.cn: 这个前缀表示向下或离开，因此复合词描绘的是沿路径向下的移动。

items.en: The Latin verb meant to lead down or to draw off, and also to derive one thing from another.
items.cn: 这个拉丁动词意为向下引领或引出，也指由一事物导出另一事物。

items.en: Medieval logic fixed the word for the step from general premises to a particular conclusion.
items.cn: 中世纪逻辑学把这个词固定为从一般前提走向具体结论的那一步。

items.en: English borrowed it in the sixteenth century, when logic and rhetoric were school subjects.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪借入，当时逻辑与修辞是学校科目。

items.en: Detection, mathematics and language teaching each gave the old step a new kind of premise.
items.cn: 侦查、数学与语言教学各自给这古老的一步配上新种类的前提。

note.en: The first group shares the leading root or its English forms; the second group names nearby kinds of reasoning and seeing. Deduce moves along a chain from premises to a conclusion, while discern grasps something faint or hidden by looking closely, so a chain of steps and an act of perception must be kept apart.
note.cn: 第一组共享引领词根或其英语形式；第二组是相邻的推理与察看。本词沿前提链一步步走向结论，辨察类词则靠细看抓住模糊或隐蔽之物，推理链与感知动作必须分开。

entries.definition: The conclusion drawn, and also the sum taken away from a total.
entries.definitionCN: 推出的结论，也指从总额中扣除的数额。

entries.definition: Of reasoning that starts from general rules, the opposite of inductive.
entries.definitionCN: 指从一般规则出发的推理，与归纳相对。

entries.definition: Able to be worked out from what is given.
To subtract an amount; the money sense split off from the reasoning sense.
entries.definitionCN: 减去一笔数额；金额义从推理义分出来。

entries.definition: To reach a conclusion from evidence; it does not require a formal chain of steps.
entries.definitionCN: 由证据得出结论；不要求正式的步骤链。

entries.definition: To arrive at a final judgement; it names the end, not the path.
entries.definitionCN: 得出最终判断；指终点，而非路径。

entries.definition: To obtain something from a source, often a formula or a word.
entries.definitionCN: 从某个来源得到某物，常指公式或词语。

entries.definition: To think logically in general; it may move in either direction.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指合乎逻辑地思考；可向任一方向进行。

entries.definition: To find an answer by thinking; the plain everyday phrase behind the formal verb.
entries.definitionCN: 靠思考找出答案；是正式动词背后平实的日常说法。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the leading root, the real family and the prepositions that mark the premise.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用引领词根、真实同族词，以及标记前提的介词。

normal.en: The root means to lead, so the verb is to be led from evidence down to a conclusion.
normal.cn: 词根意为引领，动词就是由证据被领到结论。

normal.en: The family runs deduction, deductive, deducible and the money verb deduct.
normal.cn: 同族词有推论、演绎的、可推断的，以及表示扣除的同根动词。

normal.en: The preposition is from: one deduces something from something else.
normal.cn: 介词用「由」：由某物推出另一物。

normal.en: Logic makes the step formal, and mathematics makes it visible line by line.
normal.cn: 逻辑使这步正式化，数学使它在每一行上可见。

normal.en: The detective sense is the most vivid: clues as premises written in matter.
normal.cn: 侦探义最生动：线索是用物质写成的前提。

abstract.en: Picture a path of stepping stones that only appears one stone at a time.
abstract.cn: 想象一条踏脚石小路，每次只浮现一块石头。

abstract.en: Picture a locked box whose key is the shape of the lid, not a separate object.
abstract.cn: 想象一只锁箱，钥匙的形状就藏在盖子上，而不是另一件东西。

abstract.en: Picture a rope ladder let down rung by rung, each rung held by the one above.
abstract.cn: 想象一架绳梯逐级放下，每一级都由上面一级吊住。

examples.en: From the silence in the room she deduced that the news was bad.
examples.cn: 从屋里的沉默，她推断消息不好。

examples.en: We can deduce the age of the rock from the fossils in it.
examples.cn: 我们可以从岩石中的化石推断其年代。

examples.en: The rule can be deduced from a handful of examples.
examples.cn: 这条规律可以从少数几个例子推出。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「得」加「丢斯」——顺着脚印一级级往下领，最后领出结论：推断

root: 拉丁语「向下」前缀加「引领」动词构成「向下引出、导出」，中世纪逻辑学固定为「演绎推出」，十六世纪进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all lead from something given to something concluded: evidence, premises, an origin, a context, data, clues, axioms and a theory's consequences.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都是从已给之物走向结论：证据、前提、来源、语境、数据、线索、公理与理论的后果。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a line of footprints running to a low wall while a watcher follows them step by step to the conclusion.
core.cn: 核心意象：一串脚印从泥地延伸到矮墙下，看的人顺着痕迹一步步把结论领出来。

branches.en: THE CLUES: reasoning from evidence, and reconstructing an event from physical traces.
branches.cn: 线索：由证据推理，以及由实物痕迹重建事件。

branches.en: THE FORMAL CHAIN: a conclusion drawn from premises, and the consequences of a theory.
branches.cn: 形式链：由前提推出结论，以及理论的必然后果。

branches.en: THE ORIGIN: a custom or a word traced back along a chain.
branches.cn: 来源：沿着链条反推的习俗或词语。

branches.en: THE CONTEXT: a meaning recovered from the surrounding words.
branches.cn: 语境：由周围词语复原出的含义。

branches.en: THE RULE AND THE FORMULA: a pattern drawn from data and a result derived in mathematics.
branches.cn: 规律与公式：由数据抽出的模式，以及数学中导出的结果。

intro.en: Deduce is a Latin verb of leading down, and its family supplies the noun of the conclusion, the adjective of the method and a separate verb for subtraction.
intro.cn: 本词是一个表示向下引领的拉丁动词，其词族提供表示结论的名词、描述方法的形容词，以及一个表示扣除的独立动词。

latinIntro.en: Latin ducere and the prefix de- form the verb; the English endings were added later.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语中表示引领的动词与表示向下的前缀构成这个动词，英语词尾是后加的。

items.exampleCN: 它给这个移动以向下的方向。

items.example: The root supplies the pulling of the mind along.
items.exampleCN: 词根提供心智被一路牵引之意。

items.example: The verb is the direct source of the English word.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是英语词的直接来源。

items.example: English shortened the Latin verb to its modern shape.
items.exampleCN: 英语把拉丁动词缩短为现代形式。

items.example: It builds the noun for the conclusion and for subtraction.
items.exampleCN: 它构成表示结论与扣除的名词。

items.example: It builds the adjective for the method of reasoning.
items.exampleCN: 它构成描述推理方法的形容词。

items.example: It builds the adjective for what can be worked out.
items.exampleCN: 它构成描述可被推出的形容词。

items.example: It builds the noun for the statements one starts from.
items.exampleCN: 它构成表示出发时所依据的陈述的名词。

items.example: It builds the verb for drawing a final judgement together.
items.exampleCN: 它构成表示把判断收拢起来的动词。

definition_zh: v. 减去；扣除（款项、分数等）
definition_en: to take away an amount or part from a total
core_image: 一张工资单上，总额下面划掉几行，剩下的才是到手的数
scene: 会计从总额里扣掉税款。They deduct tax from the total.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：deduct 指从总额中扣除；句意是他们从总额里扣掉税款。

senses.title: Take money off a total
senses.definition: to remove an amount of money from a total
senses.definitionCN: 从总额中去掉一笔钱
senses.example: They deduct tax from the total.
senses.exampleCN: 他们从总额里扣掉税款。
senses.why: A line crossed out on a pay slip.
senses.whyCN: 工资单上被划掉的一行。

senses.title: Take away points or marks
senses.definition: to remove points or marks as a penalty
senses.definitionCN: 作为处罚去掉分数
senses.example: The judge deducted two points.
senses.exampleCN: 裁判扣掉了两分。
senses.why: A score lowered by a written stroke.
senses.whyCN: 一笔划下去，分数就低了。

senses.title: Subtract in arithmetic
senses.definition: to take one number away from another
senses.definitionCN: 从一个数里去掉另一个数
senses.example: Deduct the discount before you pay.
senses.exampleCN: 付款前先减去折扣。
senses.why: A pile made smaller by removing some.
senses.whyCN: 拿走一些，堆就变小了。

intro.en: Deduct comes from Latin deducere, to lead away, from de- plus ducere, to lead.
intro.cn: deduct 源自拉丁语 deducere（领走），由 de- 加 ducere（引领）构成。

items.en: Ducere meant to lead.
items.cn: ducere 意为引领。

items.en: Deducere meant to lead away or draw down.
items.cn: deducere 意为领走或往下引。

items.en: Deductus was the past participle of deducere.
items.cn: deductus 是 deducere 的过去分词。

items.en: Deduct entered English for taking away an amount.
items.cn: 十五世纪 deduct 以扣除数额义进入英语。

items.en: Deduct also carried the sense of inferring.
items.cn: 十六世纪 deduct 也带有推断的含义。

items.en: Deduct settled on the money sense in accounts.
items.cn: 十九世纪 deduct 在账目上固定为扣款义。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the duct- leading root; the near-meaning group names taking away.
note.cn: 形近组共享 duct-（引领）词根；近义组都是「拿走一部分」的说法。

normal.en: De- means away.

normal.en: Deduct leads money away.

normal.en: A pay slip shows the deducted line.

sensesIntro.cn: 同一道划掉的线：钱、分数与数字。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a line crossed out on a pay slip so the total shrinks
core.cn: 核心意象：工资单上划掉一行，总额随之变小

branches.en: Both remove a counted amount as a charge or penalty.

intro.en: Deduct is de- plus ducere; the leading root builds many direction words.

latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 ducere 意为引领，trahere 意为拉。

definition_zh: adj. 可扣除的；可减去的 n.（保险）免赔额；自付额
definition_en: that can be taken away from a total, especially from tax; as a noun, the amount you pay before insurance covers the rest
core_image: 一张税表上标着「这一栏可以减掉」，另一张保单上标着「这一段自己付」
scene: 这笔开支是可以抵税的。The expense is deductible from tax.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：deductible 指可以从税里扣除；句意是这笔开支可以抵税。

senses.title: Allowed against tax
senses.definition: that may be taken away from taxable income
senses.definitionCN: 可以从应税收入中减去的
senses.example: The expense is deductible from tax.
senses.exampleCN: 这笔开支可以抵税。
senses.why: A column marked as removable on a tax form.
senses.whyCN: 税表上被标为可去掉的一栏。

senses.title: Allowed from any total
senses.definition: that may be taken away from any total or score
senses.definitionCN: 可以从任何总额或分数中减去的
senses.example: The fee is deductible from the final bill.
senses.exampleCN: 这笔费用可从最终账单中扣除。
senses.why: A line the rules allow you to cross out.
senses.whyCN: 规则允许你划掉的一行。

senses.title: The part you pay first
senses.definition: the amount you pay yourself before insurance pays
senses.definitionCN: 保险赔付之前由你自己承担的金额
senses.example: The policy has a deductible of five hundred.
senses.exampleCN: 这份保单有五百的免赔额。
senses.why: A threshold the insurer will not cross.
senses.whyCN: 一道保险公司不肯跨过的门槛。

items.en: Ducere meant to lead.

normalIntro.en: Deductible is deduct plus -ible: able to be led away from the total.
normalIntro.cn: deductible 就是 deduct 加 -ible：可以从总额里被领走的。

normal.en: Deduct means to take away.
normal.cn: deduct 意为扣除。

normal.en: The suffix -ible means able to be.
normal.cn: 后缀 -ible 意为可以被。

normal.en: Deductible can be taken off.
normal.cn: deductible 是可以被减掉的。

normal.en: Tax forms list deductible items.
normal.cn: 税表列出可扣除的项目。

normal.en: Insurance asks for a deductible first.
normal.cn: 保险先要你付免赔额。

abstract.en: A column marked as removable on a tax form.
abstract.cn: 税表上被标为可去掉的一栏。

abstract.en: A line the rules allow you to cross out.
abstract.cn: 规则允许你划掉的一行。

abstract.en: A threshold the insurer will not cross.
abstract.cn: 一道保险公司不肯跨过的门槛。

examples.en: Charity gifts are tax deductible here.
examples.cn: 在这里慈善捐赠可以抵税。

examples.en: The deductible on this policy is quite low.
examples.cn: 这份保单的免赔额相当低。

examples.en: Keep receipts for every deductible expense.
examples.cn: 保留每一笔可扣除开支的收据。

dict_mnemonic.text: deductible 谐音「弟大克特博」——不如记 deduct（扣除）＋ ible（可以）＝「可以被扣掉的」，税务上指可抵税，保险上指自付额。

root: 拉丁语 ducere（引领）→ deducere（领走）→ 英语 deduct（扣除）＋ -ible（可以）→ deductible

sensesIntro.en: One removable line: against tax, against a bill, and the part you pay.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一道可去掉的线：抵税、抵账单，以及你自己付的那一段。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a column on a form marked as removable, and a threshold you must cross yourself
core.cn: 核心意象：表格上被标为可去掉的一栏，以及一道必须自己跨过的门槛

branches.en: A column marked as removable on a tax form.
branches.cn: 税表上被标为可去掉的一栏。

branches.en: A line the rules allow you to cross out.
branches.cn: 规则允许你划掉的一行。

branches.en: A threshold the insurer will not cross.
branches.cn: 一道保险公司不肯跨过的门槛。

branches.en: Both name what the rules permit you to take away.
branches.cn: 两者都指规则允许你减掉的部分。

branches.en: Both are a share of a total kept apart from the rest.
branches.cn: 两者都是从总额中单独划出来的一份。

intro.en: Deductible is deduct plus -ible; the leading root and the ability suffix build many words.
intro.cn: deductible 由 deduct 加 -ible 构成；引领词根与「可以」后缀造出许多词。

latinIntro.en: Latin ducere means to lead and licere means to be permitted.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 ducere 意为引领，licere 意为被允许。

definition_zh: v. 认为；视作；把…看作；持某种看法
definition_en: to regard or consider something in a particular way
core_image: 一个人在心里给某件事贴上一张标签，然后按这张标签行事
scene: 委员会认为这份申请合格。The committee deemed the application valid.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：deem 指正式认定；句意是委员会认定这份申请合格。

pos.zh: 认为；视作；把…看作；持某种看法

senses.title: Judge formally
senses.definition: to decide officially that something has a quality
senses.definitionCN: 正式判定某物具有某种性质
senses.example: The committee deemed the application valid.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会认定这份申请合格。
senses.why: A label stamped on a file by authority.
senses.whyCN: 权威在档案上盖下一个标签。

senses.title: Hold an opinion
senses.definition: to consider something in a stated way
senses.definitionCN: 以某种方式看待某事
senses.example: I deem it wise to wait.
senses.exampleCN: 我认为等待是明智的。
senses.why: A private scale tipping one way.
senses.whyCN: 心里那杆秤倒向一边。

senses.title: Treat as if it were
senses.definition: to treat something as having a status it may not have
senses.definitionCN: 把某物当作具有某种身份来对待
senses.example: Silence is deemed consent here.
senses.exampleCN: 在这里沉默被视为同意。
senses.why: A blank box filled in by the rules.
senses.whyCN: 一个空栏被规则自动填上。

intro.en: Deem comes from Old English deman, to judge, from dom, judgement or doom.
intro.cn: deem 源自古英语 deman（判断），来自 dom（判决、厄运）。

items.en: Dom meant judgement or a decree.
items.cn: dom 意为判决或法令。

items.en: Deman meant to judge or decide.
items.cn: deman 意为判断或裁定。

items.en: Demen carried the sense into Middle English.
items.cn: demen 把这个含义带入中古英语。

items.en: Deem settled as the modern spelling.
items.cn: 十四世纪 deem 定为现代拼法。

items.en: Deem was common in legal and formal writing.
items.cn: 十六世纪 deem 常见于法律与正式文书。

items.en: Deem remains formal for consider or regard.
items.cn: 如今 deem 仍是 consider 的正式说法。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the dee- opening; the near-meaning group names ways of judging.
note.cn: 形近组共享 dee- 的开头；近义组都是「作出判断」的说法。

entries.definition: Extending far down or in.
A wild animal with hooves and often antlers.
A terrible fate that cannot be avoided.
To think about something carefully.
To think of someone or something in a stated way.
To form an opinion or give a decision.
To think or suppose something.

normalIntro.en: Deem is from dom, judgement: put a judgement on something.
normalIntro.cn: deem 来自 dom（判决）：给某事下一个判断。

normal.en: Dom meant judgement in Old English.
normal.cn: 古英语 dom 意为判决。

normal.en: Doom keeps the same root.
normal.cn: doom 保留同一个词根。

normal.en: Deem is to judge in the mind.
normal.cn: deem 是在心里下判断。

normal.en: A committee deems a plan fit.
normal.cn: 委员会认定方案合适。

normal.en: Silence is deemed consent.
normal.cn: 沉默被视为同意。

abstract.en: A label stamped on a file by authority.
abstract.cn: 权威在档案上盖下一个标签。

abstract.en: A private scale tipping one way.
abstract.cn: 心里那杆秤倒向一边。

abstract.en: A blank box filled in by the rules.
abstract.cn: 一个空栏被规则自动填上。

examples.en: The work was deemed complete on Friday.
examples.cn: 这项工作于周五被认定完成。

examples.en: She deemed it unnecessary to reply.
examples.cn: 她认为没有必要回复。

examples.en: Any unmarked box is deemed empty.
examples.cn: 任何未标记的箱子都视为空的。

dict_mnemonic.text: deem 谐音「弟姆」——不如记它和 doom（厄运、判决）同根：本义就是「下判决」，引申为「认为、视作」。

root: 古英语 dom（判决）→ deman（判断）→ 中古英语 demen → 英语 deem

sensesIntro.en: One label in the mind: a verdict, an opinion and an assumed status.
sensesIntro.cn: 心里的同一张标签：裁定、看法与被默认的身份。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a label stuck on a thing in the mind, then acted on as true
core.cn: 核心意象：在心里给某物贴上标签，然后当作事实去行事

branches.en: A label stamped on a file by authority.
branches.cn: 权威在档案上盖下一个标签。

branches.en: A private scale tipping one way.
branches.cn: 心里那杆秤倒向一边。

branches.en: A blank box filled in by the rules.
branches.cn: 一个空栏被规则自动填上。

branches.en: Both are a judgement reached, one public and one private.
branches.cn: 两者都是作出的判断，一个公开一个私下。

branches.en: Both let a status stand without further proof.
branches.cn: 两者都让一种身份无需进一步证明就成立。

intro.en: Deem is from dom; the judging family builds words for verdicts and opinions.
intro.cn: deem 来自 dom；判断这个家族造出许多裁定与看法类词。

latinIntro.en: Latin judicare means to judge and sentire means to feel.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 judicare 意为判断，sentire 意为感觉。

definition_zh: 击败；使落空；失败
definition_en: to win against an opponent, or to make a plan fail; also a loss in a contest
core_image: 对手低下头，慢慢走出场地
scene: 终场哨响，主队球员垂着头走向更衣室，看台上没有一个人说话。The young team defeated the champions by one goal.
sceneCN: 这里 defeat 指「击败」（第 1 个义项：在比赛或争斗中战胜对手）；句意是这支年轻队伍以一球之差战胜了冠军队。

senses.title: Win a contest against someone
senses.definition: to win a victory over an opponent in a game, battle or election
senses.definitionCN: 在比赛、战斗或选举中战胜对手
senses.example: Our team defeated the visitors by two goals.
senses.exampleCN: 我们队以两球战胜了客队。
senses.why: A contest ends the moment one side can no longer answer.
senses.whyCN: 比赛在一方再也还不了手的那一刻就结束了。

senses.title: Make a hope or plan fail
senses.definition: to cause a plan, hope or purpose to come to nothing
senses.definitionCN: 使计划、希望或目的无法实现
senses.example: The heavy rain defeated our plan for a picnic.
senses.exampleCN: 大雨让我们的野餐计划落空了。
senses.why: A plan can be beaten just as a person can be beaten.
senses.whyCN: 计划也会像人一样被打败。

senses.title: A loss in a contest
senses.definition: the fact of losing a game, battle or election
senses.definitionCN: 在比赛、战斗或选举中输掉的事实
senses.example: The defeat left the players silent in the changing room.
senses.exampleCN: 这场失败让球员们在更衣室里一言不发。
senses.why: Every victory leaves behind a second word for the other side.
senses.whyCN: 每一场胜利，都会给另一方留下另一个词。

intro.en: Defeat came to English through French, but its pieces are Latin: dis- meaning apart and facere meaning to do.
intro.cn: defeat 经法语进入英语，但零件是拉丁的：dis- 表示分开，facere 表示做。

items.en: Disfacere meant to undo or destroy what had been made.
items.cn: disfacere 意为把做好的东西拆掉、毁掉。

items.en: Desfait named the state of being undone.
items.cn: desfait 指被拆散、被毁掉的状态。

items.en: English took the word as a noun for a lost battle.
items.cn: 英语把它借来，作名词指一场打输的仗。

items.en: The verb grew beside the noun and took over the action.
items.cn: 动词在旁边长出来，接过「打败」这个动作。

items.en: A team can defeat a rival, and a problem can defeat a plan.
items.cn: 如今队伍能击败对手，难题也能让计划落空。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the de- opening, and the meaning group moves from beating someone to mastering a difficulty.
note.cn: 形近组都以 de- 开头，近义组则从打赢对手一路走到克服困难。

entries.definition: a fault that makes something imperfect
to protect someone from harm
the act of guarding against attack
to win against someone in a game
to take control of a place by force
entries.definitionCN: 用武力占领并控制某地

entries.definition: to deal with a difficulty successfully

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with the whistle at the end of a match and end with a plan that never happened.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从比赛结束的哨声开始，落到一个没能实现的计划。

normal.en: The scoreboard is honest: it says who answered last.
normal.cn: 记分牌最诚实，它只写谁最后还了手。

normal.en: A team can be beaten, and so can a good idea.
normal.cn: 队伍会被打败，好主意也一样。

normal.en: Rain does not argue with a picnic; it simply defeats it.
normal.cn: 大雨不和野餐争论，它直接把野餐毁掉。

normal.en: In defeat a crowd learns the sound of its own silence.
normal.cn: 在失败里，人群听见了自己沉默的声音。

normal.en: Defeat and defend are twins: one takes the field, one guards it.
normal.cn: defeat 和 defend 像双胞胎：一个上场攻，一个守家门。

abstract.en: Picture a flag folded and carried off the field.
abstract.cn: 想象一面旗被叠好，带离场地。

abstract.en: Picture a picnic basket still packed while rain hits the window.
abstract.cn: 想象雨打着窗，野餐篮还原封未动。

abstract.en: Picture a head lowered just enough to be seen.
abstract.cn: 想象一个头低下去，刚好让人看见。

examples.en: Our team defeated the visitors by two goals.
examples.cn: 我们队以两球战胜了客队。

examples.en: The rain defeated our plan for a picnic.
examples.cn: 大雨让我们的野餐计划落空了。

examples.en: After the defeat, the coach spoke to each player alone.
examples.cn: 失败之后，教练单独和每个球员谈了话。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 defeat 记成「敌废」：de 开头像「得」，对手被打得彻底废掉，这一仗就是击败。

root: 来自拉丁语 disfacere，由 dis-（分开）与 facere（做）组成，本义是把做好的东西拆掉、毁掉；经古法语 desfait 进入英语。它先指打输一场仗的结果，十六世纪起动词用法兴盛，后来又引申为让计划、希望落空。

sensesIntro.en: From a rival who cannot answer, to a plan that cannot happen, to the word for losing.
sensesIntro.cn: 从再也还不了手的对手，到无法实现的计划，再到表示输掉的那个词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one side walks off the field with a lowered head.
core.cn: 核心意象：一方低着头走出场地。

branches.en: The first sense is a rival who can no longer answer.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是再也还不了手的对手。

branches.en: The same force applied to a plan leaves it undone.
branches.cn: 同样的力量落到计划上，计划就做不成了。

branches.en: Seen from the other side, the same event is called a loss.
branches.cn: 从另一方看，同一件事就叫失败。

branches.en: One word serves both winner and loser, depending on who speaks.
branches.cn: 同一个词同时给赢家和输家，看是谁在说。

branches.en: Both senses describe something that stopped before it finished.
branches.cn: 两个义项都指没走完就停下来的事。

intro.en: Defeat grows a small family of nouns about giving up and adjectives about never being beaten.
intro.cn: defeat 长出一小族词：有表示放弃的名词，也有表示不曾被击败的形容词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is facere, to do, with the prefix dis- meaning apart.
latinIntro.cn: 它的拉丁词基是 facere（做），前缀 dis- 表示分开。

items.meaning: to win against, or a loss
items.example: They feared defeat more than pain.
items.exampleCN: 他们怕失败胜过怕痛苦。

items.meaning: the habit of expecting to lose
items.exampleCN: 失败主义在营地里蔓延。

items.meaning: a person who expects to lose
items.example: He was called a defeatist for doubting the plan.
items.exampleCN: 他因为怀疑计划被人叫作失败主义者。
这位拳手以不败之身退役。
没有哪支军队是无法战胜的。

items.example: The champion looked defeatable that night.
items.exampleCN: 那晚冠军看上去是可以被击败的。

items.meaning: the one who wins against another
items.example: He met his defeater the next season.
items.exampleCN: 下个赛季他遇上了击败过他的人。

definition_zh: 缺陷；缺点；叛逃
definition_en: a fault that makes something imperfect; also to leave one's country or group for another
core_image: 新杯子对着光一转，杯壁上现出一道细纹
scene: 质检员把杯子举到灯下，慢慢转了一圈，忽然停住了手。The inspector found a defect in the glass.
sceneCN: 这里 defect 指「缺陷」（第 1 个义项：产品上的瑕疵）；句意是质检员在这只玻璃杯上发现了瑕疵。

senses.title: A fault in a made thing
senses.definition: a small fault that spoils the working of a product
senses.definitionCN: 使产品不能正常使用的小毛病
senses.example: The inspector found a defect in the glass.
senses.exampleCN: 质检员在这只玻璃杯上发现了缺陷。
senses.why: A flaw shows itself only when the light is right.
senses.whyCN: 瑕疵只有在光线对的时候才露出来。

senses.title: A weakness in a person or plan
senses.definition: a weakness in character, argument or arrangement
senses.definitionCN: 性格、论证或安排上的薄弱之处
senses.example: There is one defect in your argument.
senses.exampleCN: 你的论证里有一处漏洞。
senses.why: What breaks a thing is the same whatever the thing is.
senses.whyCN: 弄坏东西的那个原因，放在哪儿都一样。

senses.title: Leave one side for another
senses.definition: to abandon one's country or group and join the opposite side
senses.definitionCN: 离开自己的国家或团体，投向对立一方
senses.example: He defected to the neighbouring country in secret.
senses.exampleCN: 他秘密叛逃到了邻国。
senses.why: A person with a crack in loyalty simply walks away.
senses.whyCN: 忠诚上有了裂缝的人，就抬脚走开了。

intro.en: Defect comes from Latin deficere, to fail or desert, built from de- away and facere to do.
intro.cn: defect 来自拉丁语 deficere（做不好、离开），由 de-（离开）与 facere（做）组成。

items.en: Deficere meant to be lacking or to fall away from a duty.
items.cn: deficere 意为缺少，或从职守上退开。

items.en: Defectus named a gap, a failure or a desertion.
items.cn: defectus 指缺口、失误或背离。

items.en: English took it first as a noun for something missing.
items.cn: 英语先把它作名词，指缺失的东西。

items.en: The verb appeared with the sense of deserting a side.
items.cn: 动词用法出现，意思是背弃一方。

items.en: Today a defect is mostly a fault found in goods, plans or eyes.
items.cn: 如今 defect 多指货物、方案或眼睛上的毛病。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the defe- opening, and the meaning group names one fault in three ways.
note.cn: 形近组共用 defe- 开头，近义组则用三种说法讲同一种毛病。

entries.definition: to win against an opponent
to protect someone from attack
lacking something needed
a mark or weakness that spoils something
entries.definitionCN: 破坏事物的瑕疵或弱点

entries.definition: a mistake or a bad part in something
a failure to reach a good standard
entries.definitionCN: 未能达到应有水准之处

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a crack seen against the light and end with a man quietly changing sides.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从对着光看见的一道裂纹开始，落到一个人悄悄换了阵营。

normal.en: A perfect cup is silent; a cracked one rings differently.
normal.cn: 完好的杯子不出声，裂了的敲起来音不一样。

normal.en: Every argument has one place where it gives way.
normal.cn: 每个论证都有一处会松口的地方。

normal.en: A gap in a wall is small, but that is where the wind comes in.
normal.cn: 墙上的缝不大，风偏偏从那进。

normal.en: A soldier who leaves his post is the same word as a broken part.
normal.cn: 离开岗位的士兵，和坏掉的零件共用一个词。

normal.en: De-fect: something not done, and so not whole.
normal.cn: de-fect 拆开看，就是「没做全」，所以不完整。

abstract.en: Picture a thin line in glass that catches the light for a second.
abstract.cn: 想象玻璃里一条细线，只闪了一下光。

abstract.en: Picture a key that almost turns but never quite does.
abstract.cn: 想象一把钥匙，差一点就能转动。

abstract.en: Picture a coat left on a chair by someone who is not coming back.
abstract.cn: 想象一件外套留在椅子上，主人不再回来。

examples.en: The inspector found a defect in the glass.
examples.cn: 质检员在这只玻璃杯上发现了缺陷。

examples.en: This model was returned because of a design defect.
examples.cn: 这款因为设计缺陷被退了回来。

examples.en: There is one defect in your argument.
examples.cn: 你的论证里有一处漏洞。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 defect 记成「得废」：de 开头，fect 听着像「废掉」，东西一废，就是有缺陷。

root: 源自拉丁语 deficere（缺少、背离），由 de-（离开）与 facere（做）合成，名词 defectus 指缺口与背离。英语先借作名词表示缺失，十六世纪又生出「叛逃」的动词义，两条线都从「离开本该在的位置」长出来。

sensesIntro.en: From a crack in a cup, to a hole in an argument, to a man who walks to the other side.
sensesIntro.cn: 从杯子上的裂纹，到论证里的漏洞，再到走到对面去的那个人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thin crack that only shows in the right light.
core.cn: 核心意象：一道只在合适光线下才显出的细纹。

branches.en: The first sense is a fault inside a finished product.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是成品内部的一处毛病。

branches.en: The same missing piece, in reasoning and in character, is a weakness.
branches.cn: 同样的缺失放到论证和性格上，就是弱点。

branches.en: A person who lacks loyalty simply leaves his own side.

senses.title: The accused in a criminal case
senses.definition: the person charged with an offence and required to answer it in court

senses.example: The defendant denied every charge read aloud in court.
senses.exampleCN: 被告对庭上宣读的每一项指控都予以否认。
senses.why: The word is the present participle of the verb 'to defend', so the accused is literally the one doing the defending in the legal contest.

senses.title: The party sued in a civil case
senses.definition: the party against whom a civil claim is brought
senses.definitionCN: 被提起民事请求的一方
senses.example: The defendant company argued that the contract had never been signed.
senses.exampleCN: 被告公司辩称那份合同从未签署。
senses.why: Civil and criminal procedure share the same structure of claim and answer, so one word serves both sides of the court system.
senses.whyCN: 民事与刑事程序共享「请求—答辩」的同一结构，所以一个词就覆盖了法院体系的两侧。

senses.title: The answering party, neutrally
senses.definition: the party that must respond to any formal claim, without implying guilt
senses.definitionCN: 必须对任何正式请求作出回应的一方，不含罪责暗示
senses.example: Each defendant was given a copy of the petition.
senses.exampleCN: 每一位应诉方都拿到了一份请求书副本。
senses.why: Procedure needs a neutral label for the side that answers, and the word supplies it without the moral weight of 'guilty'.
senses.whyCN: 程序需要一个中性的标签来指作答的一方，这个词正好提供，而不带「有罪」的道德重量。

senses.title: The party carrying the burden of answer
senses.definition: the party who must meet the claim with evidence and argument
senses.definitionCN: 必须以证据和论证来应对请求的一方
senses.example: As defendant, the hospital had to show that its staff had followed procedure.
senses.exampleCN: 作为被告，医院必须证明其员工遵守了程序。
senses.why: Once a claim is filed, the burden of answering shifts to this party, so the word also marks who must produce the evidence.
senses.whyCN: 请求一旦提出，作答的责任就转到这一方，所以这个词也标记谁必须拿出证据。

senses.title: The second name in a case title
senses.titleCN: 案件名称中排在后面的当事方
senses.definition: in the style 'A v. B', the party named after the versus
senses.definitionCN: 在「甲诉乙」式的案件名称中，排在「诉」之后的那一方
senses.example: In the report the defendant appeared second in the case name.
senses.exampleCN: 在报道中，被告排在案件名称的第二位。
senses.why: Court practice fixes the order of names, and the second slot marks the party being complained against, a convention the word now encodes.
senses.whyCN: 法庭实务固定了名称顺序，第二个位置标记被投诉的一方，这个词如今就编码了这一惯例。

senses.title: A defender in older usage
senses.titleCN: 旧用法中的防守者、辩护者
senses.definition: in older texts, a person who defends a place, a cause or another person
senses.definitionCN: 在较早文本中，指守卫某地、某项事业或他人的人
senses.example: The chronicle names him as the defendant of the northern wall.
senses.exampleCN: 编年史称他为北墙的守卫者。
senses.why: Before it became a courtroom label, the participle simply meant the one defending, in war or in argument, and older writing keeps that sense.
senses.whyCN: 在成为法庭标签之前，这个分词只表示「正在防守的人」，无论战阵还是辩论，较早文本保留了这一含义。

senses.title: Anyone who must answer criticism
senses.definition: figuratively, a person or body put in the position of answering a public charge
senses.definitionCN: 比喻义上，被置于公开指控之下、必须作答的个人或机构
senses.example: The minister found himself the defendant in a public inquiry.
senses.exampleCN: 那位部长发现自己在公开调查中成了被质询的一方。
senses.why: Because the legal frame is so familiar, it transfers to public argument, where the accused side must answer before an audience.
senses.whyCN: 因为法律框架太熟悉，它便转移到公共争论中：被指控的一方要在众人面前作答。

senses.title: The responding party in a tribunal

senses.why: Courts are not the only forum, and the word travels to any body that hears a claim and expects an answer.
senses.whyCN: 法院并非唯一的场域，这个词也适用于任何受理请求并要求答辩的机构。

intro.en: Defendant is the Old French present participle of defendre, from Latin defendere 'to ward off'. The verb joins de- 'away' with fendere 'to strike', the same second element seen in offend. The deeper origin of fendere is source uncertain.
intro.cn: defendant 是古法语 defendre 的现在分词，源自拉丁 defendere「挡开」。这个动词由 de-「离开」与 fendere「击打」构成，后半与 offend 共享。fendere 的更深来源属来源不确定。

items.en: Fendere meant to strike or push. Its deeper origin is source uncertain, and the connections sometimes proposed for it are reconstructions rather than settled derivations.
items.cn: fendere 意为击打、推。其更深来源属来源不确定，偶尔为它提出的关联只是重构，并非已定的派生。

items.en: De- 'away' plus fendere gave defendere, 'to ward off, to repel, to protect'. The military image is a blow pushed aside.
items.cn: de-「离开」加 fendere 构成 defendere，意为挡开、击退、保护。军事意象是一记被推开的打击。

items.en: The same second element appears in offendere 'to strike against', the source of offend, which shows that fendere was a productive verb of striking.
items.cn: 同一个后半也出现在 offendere「撞击、冒犯」中，即 offend 的来源，说明 fendere 曾是一个能产的「击打」动词。

items.en: French defendre meant to defend, to protect and also to forbid, a range that English inherited in part through legal phrases.
items.cn: 法语 defendre 意为防守、保护，也意为禁止，这一范围部分经法律短语传入英语。

items.en: The present participle defendant meant 'the defending one' and was used as a noun in legal French for the party answering a charge.
items.cn: 现在分词 defendant 意为「正在辩护的那一个」，在法律法语中作名词，指对指控作出答辩的一方。

items.en: English dropped the military sense from ordinary speech and kept the procedural role, while the older idea survives in historical writing about defenders of a place.
items.cn: 英语在日常口语中丢掉了军事义，保住了程序角色；而「守卫某地者」的旧义仍留在历史文字里。

note.en: Group one separates the verb, the defender, the abstract case and a look-alike with a different source; group two sets the role against the other names used for people in a case.
note.cn: 第一组区分动词、防守者、抽象的案件名目，以及一个来源不同的形近词；第二组把这个角色与案中其他人的称呼作对照。

entries.definition: The act of answering a claim or protecting someone; the defendant is the person in that position.
entries.definitionCN: 指应对请求或保护他人的动作；defendant 是处于这个位置的人。

entries.definition: One who defends, often a protector; a defendant defends himself but is named by the claim against him.
entries.definitionCN: 指防守者，常含保护者意味；被告也为自己辩护，但他是按被指控的身份命名的。

entries.definition: The answer or the whole case for the accused; the defendant is the party, not the argument.
entries.definitionCN: 指答辩或被告方的整套主张；defendant 是当事方，不是论证本身。

entries.definition: Openly refusing to obey, from French defier 'to defy'; it looks like defendant but comes from a different verb.
entries.definitionCN: 公开拒绝服从，来自法语 defier「挑战、违抗」；外形像 defendant，却出自另一个动词。

entries.definition: The possessive form marking something belonging to the party, not a separate role.
entries.definitionCN: 所有格形式，表示属于该当事方之物，不是另一个角色。

entries.definition: The person charged with a crime, common in criminal reporting; defendant is the procedural term in court.
entries.definitionCN: 被控犯罪的人，常用于犯罪报道；defendant 是法庭上的程序用语。

entries.definition: The party who answers in an appeal, arbitration or divorce case; defendant belongs to first-instance court language.
entries.definitionCN: 在上诉、仲裁或离婚案件中作答的一方；defendant 属于一审法庭的用语。

entries.definition: Any party to a lawsuit, claiming or answering; defendant names only the answering side.
entries.definitionCN: 诉讼中的任何一方，原告或被告皆可；defendant 只指应诉的一方。

entries.definition: The party who brings the civil claim, the mirror image of the defendant.
entries.definitionCN: 提起民事请求的一方，正是被告的镜像。

entries.definition: The party who appeals a decision; at that stage the old labels of plaintiff and defendant give way.
entries.definitionCN: 对判决提起上诉的一方；到了这一阶段，原告与被告的旧标签就让位了。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin verb of warding off and the real procedural opposites.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的拉丁「挡开」动词，以及真实的程序对立体。

normal.en: Defendere is to push a blow away: the defendant is the one who must push the claim away.
normal.cn: defendere 是把打击推开：被告就是必须把请求推开的那个人。

normal.en: Offend and defend share the striking verb: one strikes against, the other strikes away.
normal.cn: offend 与 defend 共享「击打」动词：一个撞上去，一个挡开。

normal.en: Defender is the protector, defendant is the accused: the same verb, two directions of attention.
normal.cn: defender 是保护者，defendant 是被指控者：同一个动词，注意力朝向两个方向。

normal.en: Defiant is a look-alike: it comes from a verb meaning to defy, not from the verb of warding off.
normal.cn: defiant 是形近词：它出自意为「违抗」的动词，而不是「挡开」的动词。

normal.en: Fixed phrases show the pair: plaintiff and defendant, the defendant's plea, a co-defendant.
normal.cn: 固定说法展示这对关系：原告与被告、被告的答辩、同案被告。

abstract.en: Picture a raised hand catching a thrown object: the hand is the defendant's whole job.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手接住抛来的东西：这只手就是被告的全部工作。

abstract.en: Picture a name written second on a courtroom docket, after the versus.
abstract.cn: 想象法庭日程表上第二个写下的名字，位于「诉」字之后。

abstract.en: Picture someone standing while everyone else sits, answering a document held in one hand.
abstract.cn: 想象所有人都坐着，只有一个人站着，手里拿着文件作答。

examples.en: The defendant chose to remain silent and let the lawyer speak.
examples.cn: 被告选择保持沉默，由律师发言。

examples.en: A co-defendant agreed to testify against the others.
examples.cn: 一名同案被告同意作证指控其他人。

examples.en: The court reminded the defendant that the burden of proof had not shifted.
examples.cn: 法院提醒被告，举证责任并未转移。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「地防等」——站在被告席上，得就地防守、等着对方出招 → 被告

root: 古法语 defendant（defendre 的现在分词，意为「正在辩护的」），源自拉丁 defendere（挡开、保护）= de-（离开）+ fendere（击打）。fendere 更深来源属来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses run from the criminal accused, through the civil party sued, the neutral answering side, the bearer of the burden, the second name in a case title, the old defender, the public figure answering criticism, and the responding party in arbitration.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从刑事被告开始，经民事被诉方、中性的应诉方、承担答辩责任者、案件名称中的第二顺位、旧时的防守者、公开受质询者，最后到仲裁中的应诉方。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand raised to catch a thrown object.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只举起的手，接住抛来的东西。

branches.en: THE TWO COURTS: the same answering role serves criminal charges and civil claims.
branches.cn: 两类法庭：同一个应诉角色既服务于刑事指控，也服务于民事请求。

branches.en: THE NEUTRAL LABEL: procedure needs a name for the answering side that carries no hint of guilt.
branches.cn: 中性标签：程序需要一个不含罪责暗示的名称来指作答的一方。

branches.en: THE WEIGHT: once a claim is filed, this party must produce evidence and argument.
branches.cn: 重量：请求一经提出，这一方就必须拿出证据与论证。

branches.en: THE ORDER OF NAMES: the second slot in a case title marks the party complained against.
branches.cn: 名称顺序：案件名称的第二格标记被投诉的一方。

branches.en: THE WIDER USE: the old defender, the public figure under criticism and the party in arbitration all keep the core of warding off a charge.
branches.cn: 更宽的用法：旧时的防守者、受公众指责的人物、仲裁中的应诉方，都保留「挡开指控」的内核。

intro.en: Defendant is a Latin participle used as a noun, so its ending marks the person in the act of defending.
intro.cn: defendant 是作名词使用的拉丁分词，词尾标记正在辩护的那个人。

latinIntro.en: The verb defendere is de- 'away' plus fendere 'to strike'; the present participle defendens supplies the English form, and the same striking verb also built offend.
latinIntro.cn: 动词 defendere 是 de-「离开」加 fendere「击打」；现在分词 defendens 提供英语形态，同一个「击打」动词也构成了 offend。

items.meaningCN: 离开、去掉（前缀表示把东西推开）
items.example: The prefix points the blow away from the body.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把打击指向身体之外。

items.meaningCN: 挡开；保护（把打击推离自身）
items.example: The compound named the warding off.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合动词命名「挡开」。

items.meaningCN: 正在防守的（分词词尾标记动作进行中）
items.example: The participle named the one defending.
items.exampleCN: 这个分词命名正在防守的人。

items.structure: defendant (French participle used as a noun)
items.meaningCN: 对指控作答的人（分词名词化，由动作转为角色）
正在做某事的人（分词词尾把动作转成施事者）
items.example: A claimant is one who claims.
items.exampleCN: claimant 就是提出请求的人。

items.meaningCN: 答辩；防御（抽象名词词尾把动作转成事体）
防守者；保护者（英语施事后缀，与 -ant 的「被控方」形成对照）
items.example: The defender of the fort surrendered.

definition_zh: 防御；保卫；防御工事；辩护；防守
definition_en: the act of protecting someone or something against attack, or the means used to do so
core_image: 一道石墙横在城门之前，墙上站着持盾的守兵
scene: 山口的城堡没有护城河，只有一道厚墙挡在骑兵必经之路上。The castle's outer wall was built as a first line of defense against cavalry.
sceneCN: 这里 defense 指「抵御进攻的军事防御」（第 1 个义项：以工事或兵力阻止敌方推进）；句意为这座城堡的外墙被建成抵御骑兵的第一道防线。图中可辨识物件：石墙、城门、持盾守兵、远处骑兵。

pos.zh: 防御；保卫；防御工事；辩护；防守（美式拼写；英式拼作 defence）

senses.title: Military protection against attack
senses.definition: the organised resistance of armed forces or fortifications against an enemy
senses.definitionCN: 武装力量或工事对敌方进攻的有组织抵抗
senses.example: The castle's outer wall was built as a first line of defense against cavalry.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城堡的外墙被建成抵御骑兵的第一道防线。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant 'to ward off'; the noun names the whole activity of warding off.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁动词意为「挡开」；名词命名整个挡开的活动。

senses.title: Legal defence of a case
senses.definition: the argument and evidence presented to protect a person or position in a legal proceeding
senses.definitionCN: 在法律程序中为保护某人或某立场而提出的论证与证据
senses.example: The lawyer mounted a strong defense of the client's innocence.
senses.exampleCN: 律师为当事人的清白作了有力的辩护。
senses.why: A trial is an attack on a claim, and answering it is the same act of warding off.
senses.whyCN: 审判是对某项主张的攻击，回应它就是同一种挡开行为。

senses.title: Defensive play in sport
senses.definition: the part of a game in which a team tries to stop the opponent from scoring
senses.definitionCN: 比赛中一方力图阻止对手得分的那一部分
senses.example: Their defense held for the final ten minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的防守在最后十分钟守住了。
senses.why: Sport reuses the military frame: one side attacks, the other wards off.
senses.whyCN: 体育沿用军事框架：一方进攻，另一方挡开。

senses.title: Biological immune defence
senses.definition: the body's systems for resisting infection or damage
senses.definitionCN: 身体抵抗感染或损伤的系统
senses.example: The skin is the body's first defense against infection.
senses.exampleCN: 皮肤是身体抵抗感染的第一道防御。
senses.why: The body treats infection as an attack, so the military noun fits without metaphor.
senses.whyCN: 身体把感染当作进攻，军事名词无需比喻便适用。

senses.title: Self-defence against physical harm
senses.definition: action taken to protect oneself from immediate physical danger
senses.definitionCN: 为保护自己免受即时人身危险而采取的行动
senses.example: She took a self-defense class before moving to the city.
senses.exampleCN: 她在搬到大城市前上了一门自卫课。
senses.why: Self-defence narrows the object of protection to one's own body.
senses.whyCN: 自卫把保护对象收窄到自己的身体。

senses.title: Verbal justification of an idea
senses.definition: a spoken or written argument in support of a person, policy or belief
senses.definitionCN: 为某人、某政策或某信念作支持的口头或书面论证
senses.example: He wrote a defense of the new tax in the newspaper.
senses.exampleCN: 他在报纸上写了一篇为新税辩护的文章。
senses.why: A claim can be attacked, and answering it repeats the same warding-off.
senses.whyCN: 主张可以被攻击，回应它就是同一种挡开。

senses.title: A fortification or barrier
senses.definition: a concrete structure such as a wall, ditch or bunker built to stop an attack
senses.definitionCN: 为阻止进攻而建的墙、壕沟或掩体等实体结构
senses.example: The old defense crumbled after two centuries of rain.
senses.exampleCN: 这座旧防御工事在两百年雨水侵蚀后坍塌了。
senses.why: The abstract act hardens into a concrete wall.
senses.whyCN: 抽象行为凝固成具体的墙。

senses.title: Psychological defence
senses.definition: an unconscious mental strategy that protects a person from anxiety or painful insight
senses.definitionCN: 保护个人免于焦虑或痛苦觉察的无意识心理策略
senses.example: Humor can serve as a defense against bad news.
senses.exampleCN: 幽默可以作为面对坏消息的一种防御。
senses.why: What cannot be stopped outside can be kept outside the mind.
senses.whyCN: 外部挡不住的东西，可以挡在心灵之外。

intro.en: Defense comes from Latin defensa, the feminine of defensus, past participle of defendere 'to ward off'. The verb joins de- 'away' to fendere 'to strike'. English uses defense in American spelling and defence in British.
intro.cn: defense 来自拉丁 defensa，即 defendere「挡开」的过去分词 defensus 的阴性形式。该动词由 de-「离开」与 fendere「击打」构成。英语美式拼作 defense，英式拼作 defence。

items.en: Defendere meant 'to ward off, repel, protect' and is the source of defend, defense and defensive.
items.cn: defendere 意为「挡开、击退、保护」，是 defend、defense 与 defensive 的来源。

items.en: The prefix de- here carries the sense 'away, off', giving the compound the idea of driving something off.
items.cn: 前缀 de- 在此表示「离开、推开」，使复合词带有「把某物赶开」的意思。

items.en: Fendere 'to strike' is rare outside compounds; it also lies behind offend and fend.
items.cn: fendere「击打」很少单独出现，只见于复合词；offend 与 fend 也出自它。

items.en: Old French defense carried the noun into English in the fourteenth century, first in the military sense.
items.cn: 古法语 defense 于 14 世纪把这个名词带入英语，最初为军事义。

items.en: British English kept defence from the French form, while American English standardized defense after Webster.
items.cn: 英式英语保留法语形式的 defence，美式英语则在韦伯斯特之后统一为 defense。

items.en: Source uncertain (root): fendere is poorly attested outside compounds, and its deeper origin is reconstructed rather than recorded; the first English date is approximate. The defendere layer is secure.
items.cn: 来源不确定（词根）：fendere 在复合词之外少有记录，其更早来源属重构而非有记录的形式；英语首见年代为约数；defendere 这一层可靠。

note.en: Group one separates the noun from its spelling variant and its family members; group two separates kinds of protection by means and by setting.
note.cn: 第一组区分该名词与拼写变体、同族成员；第二组按手段与场景区分各类保护。

entries.definition: The same noun in British spelling; American texts write defense.
entries.definitionCN: 同一名词的英式拼写；美式文本写 defense。

entries.definition: The adjective describing a posture or attitude; it cannot stand for the noun itself.
entries.definitionCN: 描述姿态或态度的形容词；不能代替名词本身。

entries.definition: A person who defends; it is an agent noun, not the act.
entries.definitionCN: 指进行保卫的人；是施动名词，不是行为。

entries.definition: Able to be justified or held; it judges the case rather than naming the defence.
entries.definitionCN: 指可被辩护或可守住的；评价该主张，而非命名防御。

entries.definition: Keeping something safe from any harm; defense usually implies a specific attack to be warded off.
entries.definitionCN: 指使某物免受任何伤害；defense 通常暗示有具体进攻需要挡开。

entries.definition: The act of opposing a force; defense is the broader plan of which resistance may be one part.
entries.definitionCN: 指对抗某种力量的行为；defense 是更宏大的方案，抵抗可以是其中一环。

entries.definition: A watch kept to prevent surprise; defense can be static or active and need not involve watching.
entries.definitionCN: 指为防止突袭而进行的警戒；defense 可以是静态或主动的，不一定涉及警戒。

entries.definition: The giving of reasons; a legal defense is a structured argument, while justification is the general act.
entries.definitionCN: 指给出理由；法律上的 defense 是有结构的论证，而 justification 是一般行为。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Latin verb of warding off, the real spelling split, and the collocations that mark each sense.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁「挡开」动词、真实的拼写分歧，以及标记各义项的固定搭配。

normal.en: de- 'away' + fendere 'strike': strike the attack away.
normal.cn: de-「离开」+ fendere「击打」：把进攻打开。

normal.en: The family runs defend, defense, defensive, defender, defensible.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 defend、defense、defensive、defender、defensible。

normal.en: American defense, British defence.
normal.cn: 美式 defense，英式 defence。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: national defense, self-defense, in defense of.
normal.cn: 固定搭配有 national defense、self-defense、in defense of。

normal.en: Five arenas: army, court, field, body, mind.
normal.cn: 五个场域：军队、法庭、赛场、身体、心理。

abstract.en: Picture a wall that exists only because someone once charged at it.
abstract.cn: 想象一道墙，它的存在只因为曾有人冲向它。

abstract.en: Picture a lawyer's sentence standing where a shield would stand.
abstract.cn: 想象律师的一句话立在盾牌本该立的位置。

abstract.en: Picture a joke raised like a small shield in front of bad news.
abstract.cn: 想象一个笑话像小盾牌一样举在坏消息之前。

examples.en: The ministry spends more on defense than on education.
examples.cn: 该部在国防上的开支超过教育。

examples.en: The court heard the defense's final argument.
examples.cn: 法庭听取了辩护方的最后陈述。

examples.en: A strong defense kept the score level until the last minute.
examples.cn: 稳固的防守把比分保持到最后时刻。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「de（离开）+ fense（打）」——把进攻打开 → 防御；保卫

root: 拉丁 de-「离开」+ fendere「击打」→ defendere「挡开」→ 过去分词 defensus → 名词 defensa → 英语 defense；fendere 更早来源为重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses share one wall: an army holds a line, a lawyer holds a case, a team holds a score, a body holds off infection, and a mind holds off anxiety.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项共享同一道墙：军队守住一线，律师守住一案，球队守住比分，身体挡住感染，心理挡住焦虑。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thick wall standing between a gate and the cavalry on the road.
core.cn: 核心意象：一道厚墙立在城门与路上的骑兵之间。

branches.en: PHYSICAL WALL: troops and fortifications stop a moving enemy.
branches.cn: 实体墙：兵力与工事挡住推进的敌军。

branches.en: VERBAL WALL: argument answers an attack on a claim or policy.
branches.cn: 言语墙：论证回应针对主张或政策的攻击。

branches.en: PERSONAL WALL: a player or a person guards a score or a body.
branches.cn: 个人墙：球员守住比分，个人守住身体。

branches.en: BIOLOGICAL WALL: skin and immunity resist infection.
branches.cn: 生物墙：皮肤与免疫抵抗感染。

branches.en: MENTAL WALL: humour and other strategies keep anxiety at a distance.
branches.cn: 心理墙：幽默等策略把焦虑挡在远处。

intro.en: Defense is a Latin participle turned noun; the family adds agent, adjective and negative suffixes to the same defendere stem.
intro.cn: defense 是由拉丁分词转成的名词；该词族在同一 defendere 词干上加施动、形容词与否定后缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin defendere, defensio and fendere supply the stem, the action noun and the rare verb of striking.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 defendere、defensio 与 fendere 提供词干、动作名词与罕见的「击打」动词。

items.example: The unit defended the bridge for a week.
items.exampleCN: 这支部队守了那座桥一周。

items.meaning: the act or means of warding off
items.example: The defense held through the night.
They took a defensive position on the hill.
items.exampleCN: 他们在山上占据防御位置。

items.meaning: able to be justified or held
items.example: The claim is defensible but thin.
items.exampleCN: 这一主张可辩护，但根基薄弱。

items.example: The nestlings are defenseless for weeks.
items.exampleCN: 雏鸟在数周内毫无防备。
她是出于自卫才行动的。

items.example: The defense line ran along the river.

definition_zh: n. 敬意；尊重；（出于尊敬的）顺从、听从
definition_en: polite respect and willingness to accept the wishes or judgement of another person
core_image: 一个人微微低头让路，把对方的意见放在自己的前面
scene: 她出于敬意让他先选。Out of deference, she let him choose.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：deference 指出于尊重的顺从；句意是她出于敬意让他先选。

senses.title: Polite respect
senses.definition: polite respect shown to someone older or higher
senses.definitionCN: 对年长者或地位更高者表现的礼貌尊重
senses.example: He bowed in deference to the judge.
senses.exampleCN: 他向法官鞠躬以示敬意。
senses.why: A head lowered so another stands higher.
senses.whyCN: 一个头低下去，让另一个人显得更高。

senses.title: Yielding to the wish of another
senses.definition: willingness to accept the wishes of another person
senses.definitionCN: 愿意接受他人意愿的态度
senses.example: Out of deference, she let him choose.
senses.exampleCN: 出于敬意，她让他先选。
senses.why: A hand letting go of the steering wheel.
senses.whyCN: 一只手松开了方向盘。

senses.title: Regard for rank or custom
senses.definition: respect for rank, age or established custom
senses.definitionCN: 对名分、年资或既定习俗的尊重
senses.example: In deference to tradition, the seat stayed empty.
senses.exampleCN: 出于对传统的尊重，那个座位一直空着。
senses.why: A chair left empty for an unseen guest.
