definition_zh: 缺乏；不足；缺陷；不足额
definition_en: a lack or shortage of something needed, or a fault that makes something incomplete
core_image: 木桶侧壁缺了一块，水位低于刻度线
scene: 体检报告上有一栏偏低：Iron deficiency is common among children in the region.
sceneCN: 这里 deficiency 是「缺乏」（第 2 个义项：营养素摄入不足）；句意：该地区儿童缺铁很常见。图中可辨识物件：木桶缺口、低于刻度的水位、血检报告、铁剂药瓶、儿童身高尺。

pos.zh: 缺乏；不足；缺陷；（账目）不足额

senses.title: A lack of something needed
senses.definition: the state of not having enough of something that is necessary
senses.definitionCN: 必需之物数量不足的状态
senses.example: The report identifies a deficiency of trained staff.
senses.exampleCN: 报告指出受训人员不足。
senses.why: Latin deficere means 'to fail or be lacking', from de- 'away' and facere 'to do'. Something is missing, so the job cannot be done, and the noun names that gap.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 deficere 意为“失败、缺少”，由 de-“离开”与 facere“做”构成。某物缺失，事情就做不成，名词命名的正是这个缺口。

senses.title: A nutrient deficiency
senses.titleCN: 营养缺乏：身体缺某种养分
senses.definition: a shortage of a nutrient required for health
senses.definitionCN: 健康所需的某种营养素不足
senses.example: Iron deficiency is common among children in the region.
senses.exampleCN: 该地区儿童缺铁很常见。
senses.why: The body is a system that needs inputs; when one input falls below the needed level, the gap is named by the nutrient that is missing.
senses.whyCN: 身体是需要输入的系统；当某项输入低于所需水平，缺口就用缺失的那种营养素来命名。

senses.title: Immune deficiency
senses.titleCN: 免疫缺陷：防线缺了一块
senses.definition: a weakness or absence in the body's immune defences
senses.definitionCN: 身体免疫防线的薄弱或缺失
senses.example: The treatment is designed for patients with immune deficiency.
senses.exampleCN: 该疗法专为免疫缺陷患者设计。
senses.why: The 'gap in the wall' image becomes medical: a missing part of the defence lets infection in, so the deficiency is a structural hole rather than a low number.
senses.whyCN: “墙上的缺口”意象进入医学：防线缺一部分，感染便能进入，因此缺陷是结构性的洞，而不只是数值偏低。

senses.title: A defect in a thing
senses.titleCN: 缺陷：设计或系统里的毛病
senses.definition: a fault or weakness that makes something incomplete or ineffective
senses.definitionCN: 使某物不完整或失效的缺点或薄弱处
senses.example: The audit found a deficiency in the control system.
senses.exampleCN: 审计发现控制系统中存在缺陷。
senses.why: Deficiency can point to a missing part rather than a missing quantity: the thing is not merely low on stock, it lacks a piece it needs to work.
senses.whyCN: deficiency 也可指缺了一个部件，而非数量不足：该物不只是存量少，而是缺少工作所需的零件。

senses.title: A deficiency judgment
senses.titleCN: 不足额判决：拍卖款不够还债
senses.definition: in law, a judgment ordering a debtor to pay the balance left after property is sold
senses.definitionCN: 法律中指财产变卖后仍欠余额、判令债务人补足的判决
senses.example: The bank obtained a deficiency judgment for the remaining balance.
senses.exampleCN: 银行就剩余余额获得了不足额判决。
senses.why: Foreclosure recovers part of a debt; the rest is still missing. The legal phrase names the gap that the court orders the debtor to close.
senses.whyCN: 止赎只能收回部分债务，其余仍然缺失。这个法律短语命名的正是法院命令债务人补上的缺口。

senses.title: A revenue shortfall
senses.definition: an amount by which income falls short of what is needed or expected
senses.definitionCN: 收入低于所需或预期数额的差额
senses.example: The city faces a budget deficiency of ten million dollars.
senses.exampleCN: 该市面临一千万美元的预算缺口。
senses.why: Accounts compare what should be there with what is there. The difference is a hole in the total, and deficiency names it more formally than shortfall.
senses.whyCN: 账目把应有的数额与实际数额相比。差额就是总数上的洞，deficiency 比 shortfall 更正式地命名它。

senses.title: An audit finding
senses.titleCN: 审计缺陷：内控上的可报告问题
senses.definition: in auditing, a weakness in internal controls serious enough to be reported
senses.definitionCN: 审计中严重到需要报告内部控制薄弱之处
senses.example: The auditors listed two material deficiencies in reporting.
senses.exampleCN: 审计师列出了报告方面的两项重大缺陷。
senses.why: Audit language treats a missing control as a gap through which error can pass. The word is technical because the gap is defined by a standard, not by a feeling.
senses.whyCN: 审计语言把缺失的控制视为让错误穿过的缺口。这个词之所以技术化，是因为缺口由标准界定，而非凭感觉。

senses.title: A deficiency disease
senses.titleCN: 营养缺乏病：缺某物直接致病
senses.definition: a disease caused by the absence of a specific nutrient
senses.definitionCN: 因缺少特定营养素而直接引起的疾病
senses.example: Scurvy is a classic deficiency disease caused by lack of vitamin C.
senses.exampleCN: 坏血病是缺乏维生素 C 引起的典型营养缺乏病。
senses.why: The compound joins the gap to its consequence: remove one necessary input and the body fails in a recognizable pattern, which medicine names after the missing item.
senses.whyCN: 这个复合词把缺口与后果连起来：去掉一项必需输入，身体就以可识别的方式衰竭，医学便以缺失物来命名疾病。

intro.en: Deficiency is deficient + -cy, from Latin deficientia, built on deficere 'to fail, be lacking'. The same verb gives deficit and defect.
intro.cn: deficiency 是 deficient + -cy，来自拉丁 deficientia，建立在 deficere“失败、缺少”上。同一动词还产生 deficit 与 defect。

items.en: deficere 'to fail, run short, desert' combines de- 'away' and facere 'to do, make'. The picture is something withdrawing from where it is needed, so the task is left undone.
items.cn: deficere“失败、短缺、背离”由 de-“离开”与 facere“做、造”组成。画面是某物从需要它的地方撤走，任务便无法完成。

items.en: deficientia 'a failing, a lack' is the abstract noun. English forms deficiency with the French-Latin ending -cy, as in other -cy nouns.
items.cn: deficientia“失败、缺乏”是抽象名词。英语用法语—拉丁来源的 -cy 词尾构成 deficiency，与其他 -cy 名词一致。

items.en: English deficiency is recorded from the 17th century in medical and administrative writing. The exact first date is approximate.
items.cn: 英语 deficiency 在17世纪的医学与行政文本中已有记录。最早确切年代为约数。

items.en: The 19th and 20th centuries fixed deficiency disease and nutrient deficiency as medicine learned to identify specific missing substances.
items.cn: 19、20世纪，随着医学学会识别具体缺失物质，deficiency disease 与 nutrient deficiency 固定下来。

items.en: Deficiency judgment and budget deficiency extend the word to money: the amount by which a fund or payment falls short of what is owed.
items.cn: deficiency judgment 与 budget deficiency 把这个词延伸到金钱：资金或付款低于应付数额的差额。

items.en: The exact semantic path from 'failing' to 'structural defect' is not fully documented. The deeper PIE origin of facere is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 从“失败”到“结构缺陷”的确切语义路径没有完整记录。facere 的更早印欧语来源属重构。

note.en: The first group contains the same-root nouns that are often confused in finance and law; the second contains shortage words with different scopes.
note.cn: 第一组是同根名词，在金融与法律语境中常被混淆；第二组是范围不同的“短缺”类词。

entries.definition: The amount by which spending exceeds income; it is usually a financial figure, while deficiency can also be a defect or a nutrient lack.
entries.definitionCN: 支出超过收入的差额；通常是财务数字，而 deficiency 也可指缺陷或营养缺乏。

entries.definition: A fault that makes a product or plan imperfect; it is countable and concrete, closer to sense 4.
entries.definitionCN: 使产品或计划不完美的毛病；可数且具体，更接近第 4 个义项。

entries.definition: The adjective meaning 'lacking'; deficiency is the noun for the lack itself.
entries.definitionCN: 意为“缺乏的”的形容词；deficiency 是“缺乏”本身的名词。

entries.definition: A situation in which supply is below demand; it is usually temporary and economic.
entries.definitionCN: 供应低于需求的情形；通常为暂时的经济现象。

entries.definition: The absence of something; the most general word, without the technical or medical frame.
entries.definitionCN: 某物不存在；最通用的词，没有技术或医学框架。

entries.definition: The amount by which a target is missed; it names a figure, not a condition.
entries.definitionCN: 未达到目标的差额；命名的是一个数字，而非状态。

entries.definition: The quality of being insufficient for a purpose; it often carries a judgment of quality.
entries.definitionCN: 对某用途而言不够的性质；常带质量判断。

entries.definition: A point that can be attacked or can fail; it is broader than a technical deficiency.
entries.definitionCN: 可被攻击或可能失效的点；比技术意义上的 deficiency 更宽。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real Latin morphology, standard collocations and the deficere family.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实拉丁构词、标准搭配与 deficere 词族。

normal.en: de- 'away' + facere 'do': something has gone away, so the work cannot be done — that is the lack.
normal.cn: de-“离开”+ facere“做”：某物离开了，事情就做不成——这就是缺乏。

normal.en: deficiency, deficit and defect are siblings: a lack, its amount, and the fault it leaves behind.
normal.cn: deficiency、deficit、defect 是同胞词：缺乏、差额、以及留下的毛病。

normal.en: Learn nutrient deficiency, immune deficiency and deficiency disease; these are the medical core.
normal.cn: 记住 nutrient deficiency、immune deficiency、deficiency disease；这些是医学核心搭配。

normal.en: In finance use deficit for the shortfall; in medicine use deficiency for the missing substance.
normal.cn: 财务缺口用 deficit；医学缺失用 deficiency。

normal.en: deficient is the adjective, deficiency the noun, deficiently the adverb.
normal.cn: deficient 是形容词，deficiency 是名词，deficiently 是副词。

abstract.en: Picture a barrel with one plank missing, so the water line can never reach the mark.
abstract.cn: 想象木桶少了一块板，水位线永远到不了刻度。

abstract.en: Picture a wall with one brick pulled out, leaving a gap wide enough for a hand.
abstract.cn: 想象墙上被抽走一块砖，留下一个能伸进手的缺口。

abstract.en: Picture an invoice where the paid amount stops short of the total, leaving a visible balance line.
abstract.cn: 想象一张发票，已付金额没到总额，留下一行清晰的余额。

examples.en: Vitamin D deficiency can weaken the bones over time.
examples.cn: 维生素 D 缺乏会随着时间使骨骼变弱。

examples.en: The review found serious deficiencies in the safety procedures.
examples.cn: 审查发现安全程序存在严重缺陷。

examples.en: The fund was set up to cover a deficiency in local services.
examples.cn: 该基金旨在弥补地方服务的不足。

dict_mnemonic.text: “de（低）+ fic（做）+ iency”——该做的没做到位，桶就缺一块 → deficiency 缺乏、缺陷

root: 拉丁 deficere“失败、缺少”（de-“离开”+ facere“做”）；deficient + -cy 名词后缀，同根词有 deficit、defect。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses share one gap: something needed is not there. The gap may be a nutrient, a defence, a control, a payment or a whole missing part.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项共享同一个缺口：需要的东西不在。缺口可以是营养、防线、控制、付款，或整个缺失的部件。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a missing plank in a barrel, with the water line below the mark.
core.cn: 核心意象：木桶少了一块板，水位低于刻度。

branches.en: DEFECT: a missing part is the same gap measured in structure.
branches.cn: 缺陷：缺失的部件，是缺口在结构层面的度量。

branches.en: BODY: a nutrient below the needed level and an immune defence with a hole both let the system fail.
branches.cn: 身体：营养素低于所需水平、免疫防线有洞，都会让系统失效。

branches.en: MONEY: a deficiency judgment and a budget gap both name the balance that is still missing.
branches.cn: 金钱：不足额判决与预算缺口，都命名仍然缺失的余额。

branches.en: TECHNICAL CONSEQUENCES: an audit deficiency is a missing control; a deficiency disease is the body's failure from a missing nutrient.
branches.cn: 技术后果：审计缺陷是缺失的控制；营养缺乏病是身体因缺营养素而衰竭。

branches.en: GENERAL CORE: the plain sense covers every specialised branch, since each branch is a particular kind of 'not enough'.
branches.cn: 一般核心：平实义覆盖所有专业分支，因为每个分支都是“不够”的某种具体形态。

intro.en: Deficiency is deficient + -cy. The suffix forms abstract nouns of state; the base is the Latin verb deficere, whose de- and fac- are fossilized.
intro.cn: deficiency 是 deficient + -cy。后缀构成状态抽象名词；词基是拉丁动词 deficere，其 de- 与 fac- 已凝固。

latinIntro.en: Latin facere 'to do, make' underlies a huge family: efficient, sufficient, deficient, defect, factory, fiction and fashion. The prefix changes whether the doing succeeds or falls short.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 facere“做、造”支撑着一个庞大词族：efficient、sufficient、deficient、defect、factory、fiction、fashion。前缀决定“做”是成功还是不足。

items.meaningCN: 缺乏；缺陷（-cy 状态名词）
items.example: The deficiency was corrected by adding a supplement.
items.exampleCN: 通过补充剂纠正了这一缺乏。

items.meaningCN: 缺乏的；不足的（-ent 形容词后缀）
items.example: The diet was deficient in calcium.

items.meaning: the amount by which something falls short
items.meaningCN: 赤字；不足额（-it 分词词尾）
items.example: The budget deficit grew for a third year.
items.exampleCN: 预算赤字连续第三年扩大。

items.meaningCN: 缺陷；瑕疵（de-“离开”+ fect-“被造”）
items.example: The defect appeared after two weeks of use.
items.exampleCN: 使用两周后出现了缺陷。

items.meaningCN: 不足地；有缺陷地（-ly 方式副词）
items.example: The system performed deficiently under load.
items.exampleCN: 系统在负载下表现不足。

items.example: The new engine is more efficient.
The evidence was sufficient for a verdict.

items.meaning: a place where goods are made
items.example: The factory produces parts for turbines.
items.exampleCN: 这家工厂生产涡轮零件。

items.example: The novel mixes fiction with recorded history.
items.exampleCN: 这部小说把虚构与有记载的历史混合在一起。

definition_zh: 缺乏的；不足的；有缺陷的
definition_en: lacking something necessary, or falling short of a required standard
core_image: 一只碗底有洞，汤从洞里漏走
scene: 田里的土色发白，苗长得慢：The soil is deficient in nitrogen, so the crops grow slowly.
sceneCN: 这里 deficient 是「缺乏的」（第 1 个义项：缺少必需成分）；句意：这片土壤缺氮，所以作物长得慢。图中可辨识物件：缺口的碗、土壤剖面、枯黄作物、氮肥袋、检测试纸。

pos.zh: 缺乏的；不足的；有缺陷的（常与 in 连用）

senses.title: Lacking an essential element
senses.titleCN: 缺乏必需成分：缺少关键的那一样
senses.definition: not having enough of a substance or quality that is needed
senses.definitionCN: 所需物质或品质的数量不足
senses.example: The soil is deficient in nitrogen, so the crops grow slowly.
senses.exampleCN: 这片土壤缺氮，所以作物长得慢。
senses.why: deficere is 'to be lacking'. The adjective describes a thing whose needed part has withdrawn, so it cannot perform its function fully.
senses.whyCN: deficere 意为“缺少”。这个形容词描述某物所需的部分已撤走，因此无法充分发挥作用。

senses.title: Insufficient in quantity
senses.definition: existing in an amount too small for a purpose
senses.definitionCN: 数量太少、不足以满足用途
senses.example: The supply of trained nurses is deficient in rural areas.
senses.exampleCN: 农村地区受训护士的供给不足。
senses.why: Here the lack is numeric: the stock is below the line the task requires, so the adjective answers 'how much' rather than 'what part'.
senses.whyCN: 这里的缺乏是数值性的：存量低于任务要求的线，因此形容词回答的是“多少”，而非“缺哪部分”。

senses.title: Below a required standard
senses.titleCN: 不达标：没到规定的水平
senses.definition: falling short of a standard set by a rule, contract or examiner
senses.definitionCN: 低于规则、合同或考核者设定的标准
senses.example: The service was judged deficient in three areas.
senses.exampleCN: 该服务在三个方面被判定不达标。
senses.why: A standard draws a line, and deficiency is the space below it. The adjective turns a comparison into an official verdict.
senses.whyCN: 标准画出一条线，deficient 就是线下的空间。这个形容词把比较变成正式判定。

senses.title: Defective or incomplete
senses.titleCN: 有缺陷的：缺了部件，运转不全
senses.definition: having a fault or missing part that prevents full working
senses.definitionCN: 存在妨碍完整运作的毛病或缺失部件
senses.example: The model is deficient because it ignores feedback.
senses.exampleCN: 这个模型有缺陷，因为它忽略了反馈。
senses.why: The gap here is structural rather than quantitative: something needed for the whole to work is absent, so the object is incomplete, not merely low.
senses.whyCN: 这里的缺口是结构性的而非数量性的：整体运作所需之物缺席，因此该物不完整，而不只是数量低。

senses.title: Nutritionally inadequate
senses.titleCN: 营养不足的：饮食里缺东西
senses.definition: of a diet, lacking the nutrients needed for health
senses.definitionCN: 指饮食缺少健康所需的营养素
senses.example: A deficient diet can cause stunted growth.
senses.exampleCN: 营养不足的饮食会导致生长迟缓。
senses.why: The body needs a set of inputs; a diet missing one of them is deficient in that item, and the medical phrase keeps the preposition in.
senses.whyCN: 身体需要一组输入；缺少其中一项的饮食就在该项上 deficient，医学短语保留介词 in。

senses.title: Academically behind
senses.titleCN: 学业不达标：某项能力没跟上
senses.definition: in education, performing below the expected level in a subject or skill
senses.definitionCN: 教育中在某学科或技能上低于预期水平
senses.example: Students who are deficient in reading need extra support.
senses.exampleCN: 阅读能力不足的学生需要额外支持。
senses.why: Schools measure a skill against a grade-level line; deficiency names the distance below that line without saying the student cannot learn.
senses.whyCN: 学校按年级水平线衡量技能；deficiency 命名低于该线的距离，并不表示学生学不会。

senses.title: A dated clinical label
senses.titleCN: 旧称“智力缺陷”：现已应避免
senses.definition: an outdated and offensive label formerly applied to people with intellectual disabilities
senses.definitionCN: 旧时加于智力障碍者的过时且冒犯性标签
senses.example: The phrase 'mentally deficient' is now avoided in clinical writing.
senses.exampleCN: 如今临床写作中已避免使用 mentally deficient 这一说法。
senses.why: The word's logic is the same gap image, but applying it to a person turns a description of need into a label. Modern usage replaces it with person-first terms.
senses.whyCN: 这个词的逻辑仍是同一缺口意象，但把它用在人身上，就把对需要的描述变成了标签。现代用法以“人优先”的术语取代它。

senses.title: A deficient number
senses.titleCN: 亏数：真因数和小于本身
senses.definition: in number theory, a number whose proper divisors add up to less than the number itself
senses.definitionCN: 数论中真因数之和小于该数本身的数
senses.example: Eight is a deficient number because 1+2+4 is less than 8.
senses.exampleCN: 八是亏数，因为 1+2+4 小于 8。
senses.why: Mathematics turns 'falls short' into an exact definition: the sum of the parts is deficient, that is, less than the whole.
senses.whyCN: 数学把“不足”变成精确定义：各部分之和 deficient，即小于整体。

intro.en: Deficient is the adjective from Latin deficere, present participle stem deficient-. It shares a root with deficiency, deficit and defect.
intro.cn: deficient 是拉丁 deficere 的形容词，来自现在分词词干 deficient-。它与 deficiency、deficit、defect 共享词根。

items.en: deficere 'to fail, be lacking' is de- 'away' plus facere 'to do'. The image is a worker or supply stepping away from the task, leaving it unfinished.
items.cn: deficere“失败、缺少”是 de-“离开”加 facere“做”。画面是工人或供给从任务旁走开，留下未完成的工作。

items.en: The present participle deficiens 'lacking' supplies the stem deficient-, which English uses unchanged in the adjective.
items.cn: 现在分词 deficiens“缺少的”提供词干 deficient-，英语形容词原样使用这一词干。

items.en: English deficient appears in the 16th century, mainly in medical and scholarly descriptions of what a body, diet or argument lacks.
items.cn: 英语 deficient 于16世纪出现，主要用于医学与学术文本，描述身体、饮食或论证缺少什么。

items.en: The construction deficient in plus a noun became fixed, parallel to rich in and weak in. It names the dimension of the lack.
items.cn: deficient in + 名词的结构固定下来，与 rich in、weak in 平行。它命名缺乏的维度。

items.en: Education, law and mathematics each adopted the adjective for their own standards, from grade-level performance to deficient numbers.
items.cn: 教育、法律与数学各自采用这个形容词来表示自己的标准，从年级表现到亏数。

items.en: The exact first English use is uncertain, and the deeper origin of facere is reconstructed rather than attested.
items.cn: 最早的确切英语用例存疑，facere 的更深来源属重构而非有据可查。

note.en: The first group is the same-root set that learners mix up; the second contains adjectives of shortage with different implications.
note.cn: 第一组是学习者常混淆的同根词；第二组是含义侧重不同的“不足”形容词。

entries.definition: The noun for the lack or defect; deficient is the adjective describing the thing that lacks.
entries.definitionCN: 表示缺乏或缺陷的名词；deficient 是描述该物缺少什么的形容词。

entries.definition: A financial shortfall; it is a countable amount, not an adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 财务缺口；是可数金额，不是形容词。

entries.definition: Having a fault that makes something unusable; it stresses malfunction, while deficient can mean simply too little.
entries.definitionCN: 有使某物不可用的毛病；强调功能故障，而 deficient 可仅指数量太少。

entries.definition: Not having something; the most general word and the least technical.
entries.definitionCN: 不具有某物；最通用、最不技术化。

entries.definition: Not enough for a purpose, often with a quality judgment; broader than deficient in a specific nutrient.
entries.definitionCN: 对某用途不够，常含质量判断；比“缺某种营养素”的 deficient 更宽。

entries.definition: Not enough in amount; it measures quantity, while deficient can also point to a missing part.
entries.definitionCN: 数量不够；衡量数量，而 deficient 也可指缺部件。

entries.definition: Not reaching a required amount or distance; it is plainer and often used of money or time.
entries.definitionCN: 未达到所需数量或距离；更平实，常用于钱或时间。

entries.definition: Available only in small amounts relative to demand; it describes supply conditions, not a thing's own make-up.
entries.definitionCN: 相对需求而言供应量很小；描述供应状况，而非某物自身构成。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphology, the in-pattern and the facere family.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实构词、in 搭配与 facere 词族。

normal.en: deficient in: the preposition names the exact dimension that is missing.
normal.cn: deficient in：介词指出缺失的具体维度。

normal.en: deficere 'fail to do': the thing could not do its job because a needed part stepped away.
normal.cn: deficere“没做成”：所需的部分走开了，这东西就无法完成工作。

normal.en: Learn deficient in, nutritionally deficient and deficient number; they mark the general, medical and mathematical branches.
normal.cn: 记住 deficient in、nutritionally deficient、deficient number；分别标记一般、医学与数学分支。

normal.en: deficiency is the noun, deficient the adjective, deficiently the adverb.
normal.cn: deficiency 是名词，deficient 是形容词，deficiently 是副词。

normal.en: Avoid the dated phrase mentally deficient; use person-first language about intellectual disability.
normal.cn: 避免旧说法 mentally deficient；谈智力障碍时使用“人优先”的表达。

abstract.en: Picture a bowl with a hole in the bottom, so no amount of soup can stay at the right level.
abstract.cn: 想象碗底有个洞，无论加多少汤都到不了应有的高度。

abstract.en: Picture a chair missing one leg, standing but unable to bear weight.
abstract.cn: 想象一把缺了一条腿的椅子，立着却承不了重。

abstract.en: Picture a gauge needle that cannot reach the green zone, always stopping short.
abstract.cn: 想象仪表指针总也到不了绿色区域，永远差一截。

examples.en: The report says the bridge is structurally deficient.
examples.cn: 报告称这座桥在结构上存在缺陷。

examples.en: Children on a deficient diet are more likely to fall ill.
examples.cn: 饮食营养不足的儿童更容易生病。

examples.en: The evidence was deficient, so the case was dismissed.
examples.cn: 证据不足，因此案件被驳回。

dict_mnemonic.text: “de（低）+ fish（鱼）+ ent”——池塘里鱼太少，低得不够吃 → deficient 缺乏的、不足的

root: 拉丁 deficere“失败、缺少”（de-“离开”+ facere“做”）；现在分词词干 deficient- + -ent 形容词后缀。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses share one gap: the needed item is below the line. The line may be set by a diet, a standard, a design, a classroom, a clinic or a mathematical definition.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项共享同一个缺口：所需之物低于标准线。这条线可由饮食、规范、设计、课堂、诊所或数学定义设定。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bowl with a hole, so the level can never reach the mark.
core.cn: 核心意象：碗底有洞，液面永远到不了刻度。

branches.en: QUANTITY: stock below the line of enough.
branches.cn: 数量：存量低于够用线。

branches.en: STANDARDS: a service judged below standard and a student below grade level are both measured against an external line.
branches.cn: 标准：服务不达标与学生低于年级水平，都以外部标准线衡量。

branches.en: STRUCTURE AND LABEL: a model missing feedback is incomplete; the dated clinical label shows what happens when a gap is attached to a person.
branches.cn: 结构与标签：忽略反馈的模型不完整；过时的临床标签显示，把缺口贴到人身上会发生什么。

branches.en: MEDICINE AND MATHEMATICS: a deficient diet lacks an input; a deficient number has parts summing below the whole.
branches.cn: 医学与数学：营养不足的饮食缺输入；亏数的各部分之和小于整体。

branches.en: GENERAL CORE: every branch is a specific way of being below what is needed.
branches.cn: 一般核心：每个分支都是“低于所需”的一种具体方式。

intro.en: Deficient is a Latin present-participle adjective in -ent. The base verb deficere is fossilized, but the suffix -ent remains recognizable as an adjective ending.
intro.cn: deficient 是拉丁现在分词形容词，词尾 -ent。词基动词 deficere 已凝固，但 -ent 仍可识别为形容词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin facere 'to do, make' underlies efficient, sufficient, deficient, defect, factory and fiction. The prefixes ex-, sub- and de- mark whether the doing comes out, measures up, or falls away.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 facere“做、造”支撑 efficient、sufficient、deficient、defect、factory、fiction。前缀 ex-、sub-、de- 标记“做”是做出成果、达到要求，还是中途撤走。

items.meaningCN: 缺乏的；低于所需水平（-ent 形容词后缀）
items.example: The sample was deficient in two minerals.

items.meaning: the state or amount of lacking
items.meaningCN: 缺乏的状态或数额（-cy 状态名词）
items.example: The deficiency was measured at ten per cent.
items.exampleCN: 缺乏程度测得为百分之十。

items.meaning: a fault in what was made
items.meaningCN: 制成品上的缺陷（de-“离开”+ fect-“被造”）
items.example: The defect was found in one batch.
items.exampleCN: 缺陷在一个批次中被发现。

items.meaningCN: 不足地；不达标地（-ly 方式副词）
items.example: The pump worked deficiently at low pressure.
The process is efficient in its use of water.
The sample was sufficient for testing.
The story is presented as fact but is fiction.
items.exampleCN: 这个故事被当作事实呈现，其实是虚构。

definition_zh: n. 赤字；亏损；亏空；不足额；（能力上的）缺陷
definition_en: the amount by which something, especially money, is less than what is needed or expected
core_image: 一个水池出水口比进水口大，水位一天天往下掉
scene: 今年预算出现了赤字。The budget ran a deficit this year.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：deficit 指支出超过收入的差额；句意是今年预算出现了赤字。

pos.zh: 赤字；亏损；亏空；不足额；缺陷

senses.title: Spending beyond income
senses.definition: the amount by which spending exceeds income
senses.definitionCN: 支出超过收入的数额
senses.example: The budget ran a deficit this year.
senses.exampleCN: 今年预算出现了赤字。
senses.why: A pool draining faster than it fills.
senses.whyCN: 一个出水比进水快的水池。

senses.title: A shortfall in supply
senses.definition: an amount less than what is needed
senses.definitionCN: 少于所需数量的差额
senses.example: The region faces a water deficit.
senses.exampleCN: 该地区面临缺水。
senses.why: A shelf with fewer jars than the list asks.
senses.whyCN: 架上的罐子比清单要求的少。

senses.title: A lack in ability
senses.definition: a weakness or lack in a skill or function
senses.definitionCN: 技能或功能上的弱点或缺失
senses.example: The tests showed a deficit in attention.
senses.exampleCN: 测试显示注意力方面存在缺陷。
senses.why: A gap where a skill should sit.
senses.whyCN: 本该有一项能力的地方是个缺口。

intro.en: Deficit comes from Latin deficit, it fails, from deficere, to fall short.
intro.cn: deficit 源自拉丁语 deficit（它欠缺），来自 deficere（不足、失败）。

items.en: Facere meant to do or make.
items.cn: facere 意为做或造。

items.en: Deficere meant to fail or fall short.
items.cn: deficere 意为失败或欠缺。

items.en: Deficit is the form meaning it fails.
items.cn: deficit 是意为「它欠缺」的形式。

items.en: Deficit entered English for a financial shortfall.
items.cn: 十八世纪 deficit 以财务亏空义进入英语。

items.en: Deficit became standard in public accounts.
items.cn: 十九世纪 deficit 成为公共账目的标准词。

items.en: Deficit widened to any measured lack.
items.cn: 二十世纪 deficit 扩展到任何可测量的不足。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the fic- making family; the near-meaning group names shortfalls.
note.cn: 形近组共享 fic-（做）家族；近义组都是「不够的部分」的说法。

entries.definition: Not having enough of something.
A lack of something needed.
A fault or imperfection.
The amount by which something falls short.
A situation where there is not enough of something.
The amount by which costs exceed income.
A space or difference between two things.

normalIntro.en: Deficit is from deficere, to fall short: the amount that is missing.
normalIntro.cn: deficit 来自 deficere（欠缺）：缺掉的那一部分。

normal.en: Deficere means to fall short.
normal.cn: deficere 意为欠缺。

normal.en: Deficit is what falls short.
normal.cn: deficit 就是欠缺的那个数。

normal.en: A budget deficit means overspending.
normal.cn: 预算赤字意味着超支。

normal.en: A trade deficit means buying more.
normal.cn: 贸易逆差意味着买得更多。

normal.en: The opposite is a surplus.
normal.cn: 反面是盈余。

abstract.en: A pool draining faster than it fills.
abstract.cn: 一个出水比进水快的水池。

abstract.en: A shelf with fewer jars than the list asks.
abstract.cn: 架上的罐子比清单要求的少。

abstract.en: A gap where a skill should sit.
abstract.cn: 本该有一项能力的地方是个缺口。

examples.en: The country has run a trade deficit for years.
examples.cn: 这个国家多年来一直有贸易逆差。

examples.en: They cut the deficit by raising taxes.
examples.cn: 他们通过加税削减赤字。

examples.en: Sleep deficits affect memory.
examples.cn: 睡眠不足会影响记忆。

dict_mnemonic.text: deficit 谐音「戴菲西特」——不如记 de（向下）＋ fic（做，与 deficient 同根）＋ it＝做下来不够数，「赤字、亏空」。

root: 拉丁语 facere（做）→ deficere（欠缺）→ deficit（它不够）→ 英语 deficit

sensesIntro.en: One draining pool: money, supply and ability.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个在漏水的水池：钱、供给与能力。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a pool whose outlet is wider than its inlet, so the level keeps dropping
core.cn: 核心意象：出水口比进水口大的水池，水位一直往下掉

branches.en: A pool draining faster than it fills.
branches.cn: 一个出水比进水快的水池。

branches.en: A shelf with fewer jars than the list asks.
branches.cn: 架上的罐子比清单要求的少。

branches.en: A gap where a skill should sit.
branches.cn: 本该有一项能力的地方是个缺口。

branches.en: Both are a measured amount less than what is needed.
branches.cn: 两者都是比所需数量少的那一部分。

branches.en: Both name a lack that shows up when you count.
branches.cn: 两者都指一算就显出来的不足。

intro.en: Deficit is de- plus facere; the making and falling-short roots build many lack words.
intro.cn: deficit 由 de- 加 facere 构成；做与欠缺这两个词根造出许多不足类词。

latinIntro.en: Latin facere means to make and deficere means to fall short.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 facere 意为做，deficere 意为欠缺。

definition_zh: 定义；界定；明确
definition_en: to state the exact meaning of something, or to mark its limits clearly
core_image: 用一条细线把一片地方圈起来
scene: 老师把粉笔放下，让学生在纸上用一句话说清那个词的意思。The teacher asked us to define the word in one sentence.
sceneCN: 这里 define 指「给…下定义」（第 1 个义项：说明词的确切含义）；句意是老师要我们用一句话说清那个词。

senses.title: State the exact meaning
senses.definition: to say exactly what a word or idea means
senses.definitionCN: 准确说出一个词或概念的含义
senses.example: The teacher asked us to define the word in one sentence.
senses.exampleCN: 老师要我们用一句话说清这个词的意思。
senses.why: A meaning held in the head is not yet shared with anyone.
senses.whyCN: 留在脑子里的意思，还不算和别人共有。

senses.title: Mark the limits of something
senses.definition: to show where the edge or limit of something lies
senses.definitionCN: 指出事物的边缘或限度在哪里
senses.example: A low wall defines the edge of the garden.
senses.exampleCN: 一道矮墙划出了花园的边。
senses.why: To say what a thing is, is also to say what it is not.
senses.whyCN: 说清一样东西是什么，也就说清了它不是什么。

senses.title: Be the mark of a character
senses.definition: to be the quality that clearly marks a person or thing
senses.definitionCN: 成为清楚标示人或事物特点的品质
senses.example: Patience defines a good teacher.
senses.exampleCN: 耐心是好老师最鲜明的特点。
senses.why: The line around a thing is what lets us know it again.
senses.whyCN: 把一样东西圈起来的那条线，让我们能再认出它。

intro.en: Define comes from Latin definire, to set a boundary, from de- completely and finis end or limit.
intro.cn: define 来自拉丁语 definire（划定界限），由 de-（彻底）与 finis（终点、界限）组成。

items.en: Finis meant a boundary, the end of a field or of a life.
items.cn: finis 指边界，可以是一块田的尽头，也可以是生命的终点。

items.en: Definire meant to draw the line around a thing.
items.cn: definire 意为绕着一件事物画出界线。

items.en: Definir kept the sense of settling and deciding.
items.cn: definir 保留了确定与裁定的意思。

items.en: English used define for explaining words as well as limits.
items.cn: 英语用它既讲界限，也讲词义。

items.en: Today we define terms, borders, duties and even a style.
items.cn: 如今我们定义术语、边界、职责，甚至一种风格。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the fine ending, and the meaning group moves from naming to making plain.
note.cn: 形近组共用 fine 这个尾巴，近义组则从命名一路走到讲清楚。

entries.definition: clear and not likely to change
to refuse openly to obey
to make something purer or better
to say what something is like
to name something exactly and clearly
entries.definitionCN: 准确而清楚地指出某事物

entries.definition: to make something easy to understand

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a line drawn in the dirt and end with a word that makes a person known.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从地上画出的一条线开始，落到一个让人被认出的词。

normal.en: A field needs a fence before anyone can say whose it is.
normal.cn: 一块地要先有篱笆，才谈得上是谁的。

normal.en: To define is to draw a circle and then stand outside it to look.
normal.cn: 下定义就是画一个圈，再站到圈外看它。

normal.en: Say what a word means and you have also said what it does not.
normal.cn: 说清一个词的意思，也就说清它不是什么。

normal.en: Patience does not describe a teacher; it defines one.
normal.cn: 耐心不是描述老师，而是标示出老师。

normal.en: Finis is the end, so define puts an end to vagueness.
normal.cn: finis 是终点，所以 define 就是给含糊画上句号。

abstract.en: Picture a fingertip tracing a line in dry earth.
abstract.cn: 想象一个指尖在干土上划出一条线。

abstract.en: Picture a lamp held close so one page is bright and the rest is dark.
abstract.cn: 想象一盏灯凑得很近，一页亮着，其余都暗。

abstract.en: Picture a name written under a drawing, fixing what it is.
abstract.cn: 想象画下写着一个名字，把画的内容定住。

examples.en: The teacher asked us to define the word in one sentence.
examples.cn: 老师要我们用一句话说清这个词的意思。

examples.en: A low wall defines the edge of the garden.
examples.cn: 一道矮墙划出了花园的边。

examples.en: Patience defines a good teacher.
examples.cn: 耐心是好老师最鲜明的特点。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 define 记成「定分」：de 开头，fine 是「精细」，把意思定得精细，就是下定义。

root: 源自拉丁语 definire，由 de-（彻底）与 finis（界限、终点）组成，本义是绕着一块地画出界线；经古法语 definir 进入英语。界线之内是它，界线之外不是它，所以这个词既表示划定范围，也表示说清含义。

sensesIntro.en: From a line around a field, to a line around a word, to the line that marks a person.
sensesIntro.cn: 从圈住一块田的线，到圈住一个词的线，再到标示一个人的那条线。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thin line drawn around a piece of ground.
core.cn: 核心意象：一圈细线把一块地围起来。

branches.en: The first sense draws the line around a word's meaning.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是把线画在一个词的含义周围。

branches.en: The same line, laid on ground, settles a border.
branches.cn: 同样的线落到地上，就定下了边界。

branches.en: Laid on a person, the line marks what is most truly his.
branches.cn: 这条线落到人身上，就标出他最真的那一面。

branches.en: Meaning and border are both made by drawing limits.
branches.cn: 含义与边界都是靠划出限度做成的。

branches.en: Both senses tell us where something begins and ends.
branches.cn: 两个义项都在告诉我们事物从哪里开始、到哪里为止。

intro.en: Define has given English a whole set of words about clear limits: definition, definite and indefinite.
intro.cn: define 给英语送来一整组关于明确界限的词：definition、definite、indefinite。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is finis, a boundary, with the prefix de- meaning completely.
latinIntro.cn: 它的拉丁词基是 finis（边界），前缀 de- 表示彻底。

items.meaning: to fix the meaning or limit
items.example: The law defines the duty of the owner.
items.exampleCN: 法律界定了业主的责任。

items.example: The definition was short and exact.

items.exampleCN: 我们需要一个明确的答复。

items.example: They agreed to an indefinite wait.

items.meaning: to define again in a new way

这项任务界定得很清楚。

definition_zh: 明确的；确定的；明显的
definition_en: clear and fixed, not open to doubt; also easy to notice
core_image: 纸上一行字被框得方方正正，没有涂抹
scene: 她翻着日历，把下周的会面日期圈了两遍，却还留着一格空白。We still have no definite date for the meeting.
sceneCN: 这里 definite 指「明确的」（第 1 个义项：清楚而不含糊）；句意是我们还没有一个明确的会议日期。

senses.title: Clear and not vague
senses.definition: stated in a way that leaves no doubt about what is meant
senses.definitionCN: 说法清楚，让人对意思没有疑问
senses.example: We still have no definite date for the meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 我们还没有一个明确的会议日期。
senses.why: A word with edges can be held; a vague one slips away.
senses.whyCN: 有边的话才拿得住，含糊的话会滑走。

senses.title: Certain in one's mind
senses.definition: sure that something is true or will happen
senses.definitionCN: 确信某事为真或将会发生
senses.example: She was definite about her answer.
senses.exampleCN: 她对自己的回答很确定。
senses.why: Certainty is a room with the door closed.
senses.whyCN: 确定感就像一间关上了门的屋子。

senses.title: Easy to see or feel
senses.definition: large enough or strong enough to be noticed at once
senses.definitionCN: 大到或强到一眼就能察觉
senses.example: There is a definite change in the air.
senses.exampleCN: 空气里有一种明显的变化。
senses.why: What has edges also casts a shadow you cannot miss.
senses.whyCN: 有边的东西，投下的影子也让人没法忽略。

intro.en: Definite is the old past participle of define, so it carries the same picture of a line drawn around something.
intro.cn: definite 是 define 的古老过去分词，因此带着同样一幅「画线围住」的图景。

items.en: Definitus meant bounded, settled and brought to an end.
items.cn: definitus 意为有界的、定下的、已经结束的。

items.en: The word described a field with its corners marked.
items.cn: 这个词形容一块四角都标好的田。

items.en: Definit came into French as settled and certain.
items.cn: definit 进入法语时表示已定、确实。

items.en: English used it for answers, orders and grammar.
items.cn: 英语用它形容答复、命令和语法。

items.en: Grammar keeps the definite article for the one already known.
items.cn: 语法里仍用 definite article 指已经知道的那一个。

note.en: The look-alike group walks around the same fin stem, and the meaning group measures how sure a statement is.
note.cn: 形近组绕着同一个 fin 词干，近义组则衡量一句话有多确定。

entries.definition: to state the exact meaning of something
entries.definitionCN: 说明某事物的确切含义

entries.definition: final and not to be changed
having no end or limit
sure beyond doubt
easy to see or understand
named exactly rather than in general

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a date circled twice and end with a change in the air nobody can miss.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从被圈了两遍的日期开始，落到空气里谁也躲不开的变化。

normal.en: The definite article points at the cup you both already see.

normal.en: When the air changes, you feel it before you can name it.

normal.en: Definite and infinite are brothers, one with a fence and one without.

abstract.en: Picture a square drawn in dust with a stick.

abstract.en: Picture a hand pressing a page flat so nothing moves.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手把纸压平，什么也不许动。

abstract.en: Picture a shadow on the wall that tells you someone is near.
abstract.cn: 想象墙上一道影子，告诉你有人靠近。

examples.en: We still have no definite date for the meeting.

examples.en: She was definite about her answer.

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 definite 记成「定分你特」：de 开头，finite 是有限，界限分明，就是明确的。

root: 源自拉丁语 definitus，是 definire（划定界限）的过去分词，词根 finis 表示边界与终点。有边就有形，有形就不含糊，所以这个词从「划定的」引申出明确、确定与明显三层意思，语法上的定冠词也由此得名。

sensesIntro.en: From a bounded thing, to a closed mind, to a change too large to ignore.
sensesIntro.cn: 从有边有界的东西，到关上了门的心思，再到大到无法忽略的变化。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a line drawn neatly around a word.
core.cn: 核心意象：一圈画得整整齐齐的线，围住一个词。

branches.en: The first sense is a statement with clear edges.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是边界清楚的一句话。

branches.en: The same clarity, inside a person, becomes certainty.
branches.cn: 同样的清楚放进人心里，就是确定。

branches.en: What is clearly bounded also stands out at once.
branches.cn: 界限清楚的东西，也一眼就能看出来。

branches.en: A clear answer and a sure mind are two sides of one line.
branches.cn: 清楚的答复与笃定的心思，是同一条线的两面。

branches.en: Both senses are about things that cannot be argued away.
branches.cn: 两个义项都指没法被说没的东西。

intro.en: Definite anchors a family of words about limits: define, definition, indefinite and definitive.
intro.cn: definite 撑起一族关于界限的词：define、definition、indefinite、definitive。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is finis, a boundary, with de- meaning completely.
latinIntro.cn: 它的拉丁词基是 finis（边界），前缀 de- 表示彻底。

items.exampleCN: 这条定义适用于这种情况。
他们把任务界定得很清楚。

items.example: The definiteness of her tone surprised us.
items.exampleCN: 她语气的确定让我们吃惊。

items.example: The building stands empty for an indefinite time.
This is the definitive study of the river.
items.exampleCN: 这是关于这条河最权威的研究。

items.meaning: the word the, marking something known
items.meaningCN: 定冠词（指已知事物的 the）
items.example: Use the definite article before the noun.
items.exampleCN: 在这个名词前要用定冠词。

definition_zh: 定义；释义；清晰度
definition_en: a statement of what a word or idea means; also the sharpness of an image
core_image: 词典上一行小字，把一个词钉住
scene: 她把词典摊在膝上，指尖顺着两行小字往下滑。The dictionary gives two definitions of the word.
sceneCN: 这里 definition 指「释义」（第 1 个义项：说明词义的语句）；句意是词典给出了这个词的两条释义。

senses.title: A statement of meaning
senses.definition: a sentence that says exactly what a word or idea means
senses.definitionCN: 准确说明一个词或概念含义的句子
senses.example: The dictionary gives two definitions of the word.
senses.exampleCN: 词典给出了这个词的两条释义。
senses.why: A word without a definition is a door without a key.
senses.whyCN: 没有定义的词，就像没有钥匙的门。

senses.title: The act of marking limits
senses.definition: the act of fixing the border or scope of something
senses.definitionCN: 确定某事物的边界或范围的行为
senses.example: The definition of the study area took a month.
senses.exampleCN: 划定研究区域用了一个月。
senses.why: Before a thing can be studied, its edge must be agreed on.
senses.whyCN: 要研究一样东西，先得商量好它的边在哪儿。

senses.title: Sharpness of an image
senses.definition: the clearness of an image or sound on a screen
senses.definitionCN: 屏幕上的画面或声音清楚的程度
senses.example: The old film was restored in high definition.
senses.exampleCN: 这部老片子被修复成了高清。
senses.why: A sharp edge is what the eye and the mind both call clear.
senses.whyCN: 边缘锐利，眼睛和脑子都会说它清楚。

intro.en: Definition comes from Latin definitio, a bounding, from finis, a limit, and de-, completely.
intro.cn: definition 来自拉丁语 definitio（划定边界），出自 finis（界限）与 de-（彻底）。

items.en: Finis marked the end of a field or the close of a speech.
items.cn: finis 指一块田的尽头，也指一段话的收尾。

items.en: Definitio was the act of drawing a thing's border.
items.cn: definitio 是给事物画出边界的行为。

items.en: Definicion carried the word into law and learning.
items.cn: definicion 把这个词带进法律与学问。

items.en: English used it for the meaning given in a dictionary.
items.cn: 英语用它指词典里给出的意思。

items.en: Film and screens added the sense of a sharp picture.
items.cn: 电影与屏幕又给它添了画面清晰这一层意思。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the fin stem, and the meaning group names what a definition gives to a reader.
note.cn: 形近组共用 fin 词干，近义组则说出定义交给读者的东西。

clear and certain
to say what something means
words that make something understood
what a word or sign stands for

entries.definition: a picture made with words

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a finger running down a dictionary and end with a picture sharp enough to touch.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从沿着词典往下滑的指尖开始，落到清晰得几乎能摸到的画面。

normal.en: A definition is a small fence built around a large word.
normal.cn: 定义就是给一个大词围起来的一道小篱笆。

normal.en: Two definitions for one word mean two doors into the same house.
normal.cn: 一个词有两条释义，就是同一间屋子的两扇门。

normal.en: You cannot count what you have not first bounded.
normal.cn: 没有先划出范围，就没法数清里面有多少。

normal.en: A high definition picture is just a picture with cleaner edges.
normal.cn: 高清画面，不过是边缘更干净的画面。

normal.en: Definition is the noun that define leaves behind.
normal.cn: definition 就是 define 留下的那个名词。

abstract.en: Picture a fingertip stopping under one line of small print.
abstract.cn: 想象一个指尖停在一行小字下面。

abstract.en: Picture a rope laid on grass to mark where the tent goes.
abstract.cn: 想象草地上拉一根绳，标出帐篷该搭在哪。

abstract.en: Picture a leaf on a screen with every vein in view.
abstract.cn: 想象屏幕上一片叶子，每根叶脉都看得见。

examples.en: The dictionary gives two definitions of the word.
examples.cn: 词典给出了这个词的两条释义。

examples.en: By definition, a square has four equal sides.
examples.cn: 按照定义，正方形有四条相等的边。

examples.en: The old film was restored in high definition.
examples.cn: 这部老片子被修复成了高清。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 definition 记成「定分神」：定得分明，一句话就把词钉住，神都跑了，定义却留下。

root: 源自拉丁语 definitio，出自 definire（划定界限），词根 finis 表示边界与终点。先有「画线」这个动作，才有「划出的范围」，再有「说明词义的语句」；近代摄影与屏幕又借它表示图像的清晰度。

sensesIntro.en: From a line around a word, to the act of drawing it, to the edge of a picture.
sensesIntro.cn: 从围住一个词的那条线，到画线的动作，再到画面的边缘。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small fence built around one word.
core.cn: 核心意象：围着一个词搭起的一小圈篱笆。

branches.en: The first sense is the sentence that fences a word.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是把词围起来的那句话。

branches.en: The second sense is the act of building that fence.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是搭起这道篱笆的动作。

branches.en: On a screen, the fence becomes a clean edge.
branches.cn: 在屏幕上，这道篱笆变成了干净的边。

branches.en: A statement and the act behind it are one thing seen twice.
branches.cn: 一句话和它背后的动作，是同一件事的两种看法。

branches.en: Both senses are about making a shape stand out from its background.
branches.cn: 两个义项都是让形状从背景里站出来。

intro.en: Definition belongs to the finis family, with define, definite, definitive and indefinite beside it.

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is finis, a boundary, with de- meaning completely.

items.example: The definition runs to three lines.

senses.title: Let air out

senses.definitionCN: 把某物里的气放出来

intro.en: Deflate is de- plus flare; the blowing root builds the inflate and deflate pair.
intro.cn: deflate 由 de- 加 flare 构成；吹这个词根造出充气与放气这一对词。

latinIntro.en: Latin flare means to blow and pungere means to prick.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 flare 意为吹，pungere 意为刺。

definition_zh: 通货紧缩；放气；泄气；削减；风蚀
definition_en: a sustained fall in the general level of prices, or the act of letting air out of something
core_image: 渔村的鱼价一月比一月低，摊主把价签往下改，欠的债却一分没少
scene: 海边的渔村在萧条里过了两年，鱼价一月比一月低，摊主把价签往下改，欠的债却一分没少。 Shops cut prices again and again, and the town slid into deflation.
sceneCN: 这里 deflation 指「一般物价水平持续下跌」（第 1 个义项：整体物价持续走低、货币购买力上升）；句意为店铺一再降价，小镇滑入通缩。图中可辨识物件：下调的价签、空鱼筐、账本、紧闭的店门。

pos.zh: 通货紧缩；放气；泄气；风蚀

senses.title: A sustained fall in the price level
senses.definition: a continuing decrease in the general level of prices, so that money gains purchasing power over time
senses.definitionCN: 整体物价水平持续下降，使同样多的钱随时间买到更多东西
senses.example: Shops cut prices again and again, and the town slid into deflation.
senses.exampleCN: 店铺一再降价，小镇滑入通缩。
senses.why: The word is the mirror of inflation: the same balloon image is reversed, so the currency is pictured as being let down rather than blown up.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是 inflation 的镜像：同一个气球意象被反过来，通货被想象成放气而不是吹胀。

senses.title: The act of letting air out
senses.definition: the act of releasing air or gas from a tyre, balloon or other inflated object
senses.definitionCN: 把空气或气体从轮胎、气球或其他充气物中放出的动作
senses.example: Deflation of the damaged tyre took only a moment.
senses.exampleCN: 给受损轮胎放气只用了一会儿。
senses.why: This is the literal sense of the Latin verb: de- 'down, away' plus flare 'to blow' means to blow away or let the air out.
senses.whyCN: 这是拉丁动词的字面义：de-「向下、离开」加 flare「吹」，意为吹走或放掉气。

senses.title: A loss of confidence
senses.definition: a state of lowered spirits after a setback, as if the person had been emptied of air
senses.definitionCN: 受挫之后情绪低落的状态，仿佛人被抽空了气
senses.example: The defeat left a quiet deflation in the dressing room.
senses.exampleCN: 这场失利在更衣室里留下一种无声的泄气。
senses.why: The physical emptying of a balloon supplies a ready metaphor for morale, which the noun can carry without any economic content.
senses.whyCN: 把气球放空这一物理动作，为士气提供了现成的比喻，名词因此可以完全不带经济内容。

senses.title: A cut in scale or spending
senses.definition: a deliberate reduction in the size, cost or activity of something
senses.definitionCN: 有意缩减某事物的规模、成本或活动量
senses.example: The deflation of the program removed two of its four offices.
senses.exampleCN: 该项目缩减后，四个办事处关掉了两个。
senses.why: If blowing in expands a thing, letting air out contracts it, so the noun naturally serves any plan of shrinking.
senses.whyCN: 既然吹入使事物膨胀，放气就使它收缩，因此这个名词自然可用于任何缩减方案。

senses.title: Wind erosion of the land
senses.titleCN: 风把地表颗粒吹走的风蚀
senses.definition: the removal of loose soil or sand by wind, a geological process named after the blowing away of particles
senses.definitionCN: 风把松散土壤或沙粒吹走的地质过程，因颗粒被吹走而得名
senses.example: Deflation has stripped the dune field down to bare rock.
senses.exampleCN: 风蚀已把这片沙丘地剥到只剩裸岩。
senses.why: Geologists took the literal 'blow away' sense and applied it to wind lifting loose material off the surface.
senses.whyCN: 地质学家取了字面的「吹走」义，用来指风把松散物质从地表抬走。

senses.title: A policy of tightening
senses.definition: a government or central-bank policy that reduces demand, credit or public spending
senses.definitionCN: 政府或央行压低需求、信贷或公共开支的政策
senses.example: The deflation of credit came before the fall in output.
senses.exampleCN: 信贷的紧缩先于产出的下降。
senses.why: Policy language borrows the noun because the aim is to take air out of an overheated economy.
senses.whyCN: 政策话语借用这个名词，因为目的正是给过热的经济放掉一些气。

senses.title: Debt deflation
senses.titleCN: 物价下跌加重债务的债务紧缩
senses.definition: the process in which falling prices make existing debts heavier in real terms and force further cuts
senses.definitionCN: 物价下跌使既有债务按实值变重、并迫使进一步缩减的过程
senses.example: Debt deflation turned the slowdown into a long stagnation.
senses.exampleCN: 债务紧缩把放缓拖成了长期停滞。
senses.why: When the measure of value itself shrinks, every fixed debt grows relative to it, and the word names that self-feeding loop.
senses.whyCN: 当价值尺度本身缩小时，每一笔固定债务相对它就变重，这个词命名的正是这种自我喂养的循环。

senses.title: The deflation rate
senses.definition: a percentage expressing the pace at which the general price level is falling
senses.definitionCN: 表示整体物价水平下降速度的百分数
senses.example: The deflation rate eased to one percent in the spring.
senses.exampleCN: 通缩率在春季放缓至百分之一。
senses.why: As with inflation, the process noun comes to stand for its own measurement, so it can be attached directly to rate.
senses.whyCN: 与 inflation 一样，过程名词转指自身的度量，因此可以直接与 rate 搭配。

intro.en: Deflation is built on Latin deflare 'to blow away', from de- 'down, away' and flare 'to blow'; the economic sense was formed as the counterpart of inflation in the nineteenth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: deflation 建立在拉丁 deflare「吹走」之上，即 de-「向下、离开」加 flare「吹」；经济义是 19 世纪作为 inflation 的对立面而形成的。年代均为约数。

items.en: Flare meant 'to blow, to breathe out', the source of a small family of English words about blowing.
items.cn: flare 意为「吹、呼出气」，是英语中一小族「吹气」词的来源。

items.en: De- 'down, away' plus flare gave deflare 'to blow away, to blow off', used of wind and of emptying something by blowing.
items.cn: de-「向下、离开」加 flare 构成 deflare「吹走、吹掉」，用于风，也指吹气把某物腾空。

items.en: The English verb deflate appeared in the nineteenth century for letting air or gas out of a balloon, tyre or cavity.
items.cn: 英语动词 deflate 于 19 世纪出现，指把空气或气体从气球、轮胎或腔体中放出。

items.en: The economic noun is generally dated to the nineteenth century and was consciously coined as the opposite of inflation, reversing the same balloon image.
items.cn: 经济义名词一般认为是 19 世纪的产物，并被有意造作 inflation 的反面，把同一个气球意象反转过来。

items.en: Nineteenth-century geology applied the literal 'blowing away' sense to wind stripping loose sand and soil from the surface.
items.cn: 19 世纪的地质学把字面的「吹走」义用于风把松散沙土从地表剥走。

items.en: Because the word was built by analogy rather than inherited, its first economic use is generally placed in the nineteenth century, though the precise decade is not fixed here.
items.cn: 由于这个词是按类比而非继承造出的，其最早经济用例一般被认为在 19 世纪，确切年代此处不作定论。

note.en: The first group holds the mirror process, the verb behind it, and one look-alike with a different job; the second holds declines of prices, of inflation and of output.
note.cn: 第一组是镜像过程、其背后的动词，以及一个外形相近但作用不同的词；第二组是物价下降、通胀放慢与产出下降。

entries.definition: Prices rise and money loses purchasing power; deflation is the same mechanism running backwards.
entries.definitionCN: 物价上涨、货币购买力下降；deflation 是同一机制反向运行。

entries.definition: To let air out or to lower prices; the noun deflation names the process or its result.
entries.definitionCN: 放气或压低价格；名词 deflation 指过程或结果。

entries.definition: Describes pressure that pushes prices down; it names the force, not the decline.
entries.definitionCN: 描述把物价往下压的力量；它指力量而非下跌本身。

entries.definition: In statistics, a deflator is a price index used to strip inflation out of nominal figures; it is a tool, not a process.
entries.definitionCN: 在统计中，deflator 是用来从名义数字里剔除物价变动影响的指数；它是工具，不是过程。

entries.definition: An everyday phrase for falling prices; it may describe one good, whereas deflation means the general level.
entries.definitionCN: 日常说法，指价格下跌；可指单一商品，而 deflation 指整体水平。

entries.definition: A slowing of inflation while prices are still rising; unlike deflation, the level does not fall.
entries.definitionCN: 物价仍在上涨、只是涨幅放缓；与 deflation 不同，水平并未下降。

entries.definition: A deep and long slump in output and employment; deflation may accompany it but is a separate price phenomenon.
entries.definitionCN: 产出与就业的深重长期低迷；通缩可与之并存，但属于独立的价格现象。

entries.definition: A policy of cutting public spending; it is a chosen response, not a movement of prices.
entries.definitionCN: 削减公共开支的政策；它是主动选择的对策，不是价格运动。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: a real Latin prefix and root, a real family and real fixed phrases, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁前缀与词根、真实的同族词与真实的固定说法，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: de- 'down, away' plus flare 'to blow': to blow the air out.
normal.cn: de-「向下、离开」加 flare「吹」：把气吹走。

normal.en: The family runs deflate, deflation, deflationary, deflator, inflate, inflation.
normal.cn: 同族词串成一线：deflate、deflation、deflationary、deflator、inflate、inflation。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: price deflation, deflationary pressure, debt deflation, deflation spiral.
normal.cn: 固定说法：物价下跌、通缩压力、债务紧缩、通缩螺旋。

normal.en: Remember the pair by the prefix: in- blows up, de- lets out.
normal.cn: 用前缀记这一对：in- 往里吹，de- 往外放。

normal.en: Geology uses the literal sense: wind blowing loose sand away.
normal.cn: 地质学用字面义：风把松散沙粒吹走。

abstract.en: Picture a balloon slowly losing its shape against a wall.
abstract.cn: 想象一只气球贴着墙慢慢瘪下去。

abstract.en: Picture a price tag being crossed out and rewritten lower, twice in a month.
abstract.cn: 想象一张价签被划掉、改低，一个月里改了两次。

abstract.en: Picture a debt that grows heavier while the shop's takings shrink.
abstract.cn: 想象店里的进账越来越薄，欠的债却越来越重。

examples.en: Deflation punishes borrowers because their debts stay fixed while incomes fall.
examples.cn: 通缩惩罚借款人，因为收入下降而债务不变。

examples.en: The central bank denied that the economy was entering deflation.
examples.cn: 央行否认经济正进入通缩。

examples.en: Wind deflation has left a shallow basin in the plateau.
examples.cn: 风蚀在高原上留下一个浅盆地。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「de（向下）+ flat（气）+ ion」——把气往下放掉，越放越瘪 → 放气、通缩

root: 拉丁 deflare「吹走」= de-「向下、离开」+ flare「吹」→ 英语 deflate / deflation；经济义为 19 世纪按 inflation 反向类比造出，确切年代不作定论；地质义亦出自字面「吹走」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one reversed gesture: air is let out, the thing slackens, and the same slackening is applied to prices, to morale, to a budget, to the land, to credit and finally to a spiral of debt.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个反向动作展开：把气放掉，物体瘪下去；同一种「瘪下去」再依次用于物价、士气、预算、土地、信贷，最后是债务的螺旋。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a balloon going slack, a price tag rewritten lower, and a debt that does not shrink with it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只瘪下去的气球、一张改低的价签，以及一笔并不随之缩小的债。

branches.en: PRICE AND RATE: the falling level of prices is measured and reported as a percentage.
branches.cn: 物价与比率：下跌的物价水平被度量并报告为一个百分数。

branches.en: AIR AND SPIRIT: letting air out of a thing mirrors the emptying of confidence.
branches.cn: 气与心气：把物体放空，正映照着信心的被抽空。

branches.en: SCALE: the same release becomes a deliberate cut in size or spending.
branches.cn: 规模：同一种「放掉」变成对规模或开支的有意削减。

branches.en: LAND: wind literally blows the loose surface away.
branches.cn: 土地：风把松散的地表真的吹走。

branches.en: CREDIT AND DEBT: tightening policy meets the loop in which cheaper money makes fixed debt heavier.
branches.cn: 信贷与债务：紧缩政策遇上「钱变便宜反而使固定债务变重」的循环。

intro.en: The word is a Latin prefix, a Latin verb root and a noun suffix; the same three pieces build its mirror image and a whole small family.
intro.cn: 这个词由一个拉丁前缀、一个拉丁动词词根与一个名词后缀构成；这三段也构成它的镜像词与整个小词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin flare 'to blow' gives deflate, deflation, deflator, inflate, inflation and flatus; de- and in- mark the two opposite directions.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 flare「吹」衍生出 deflate、deflation、deflator、inflate、inflation 与 flatus；de- 与 in- 标出两个相反方向。

The root supplies the image of moving air.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根提供推动空气的意象。

items.meaning: to blow away; to blow out
items.example: The compound names emptying by blowing.

items.example: The Latin noun underlies the English form.

items.exampleCN: 平减指数从名义产出中剔除了价格变动。

definition_zh: v. 使转向；使偏斜；使弯曲；挡开；转移（批评、注意力）
definition_en: to make something change direction, or to turn attention or criticism away from yourself
core_image: 一支飞来的箭撞到盾面，斜着弹开，没有扎进身体
scene: 盾把箭挡偏了。The shield deflected the arrow.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：deflect 指使飞行物改变方向；句意是盾把箭挡偏了。

pos.zh: 使转向；使偏斜；使弯曲；挡开；转移（批评、注意力）

senses.title: Turn a moving thing aside
senses.definition: to make a moving object change direction
senses.definitionCN: 让运动中的物体改变方向
senses.example: The shield deflected the arrow.
senses.exampleCN: 盾把箭挡偏了。
senses.why: A straight flight bent by a slanted face.
senses.whyCN: 一条直线飞行被一个斜面折弯。

senses.title: Bend a beam or ray
senses.definition: to bend light, sound or a beam from its path
senses.definitionCN: 让光、声或束流偏离原路径
senses.example: The mirror deflected the laser beam.
senses.exampleCN: 镜子把激光束偏转了。
senses.why: A ray turned at a polished surface.
senses.whyCN: 一条光线在光洁表面上拐了弯。

senses.title: Turn blame or attention away
senses.definition: to direct criticism or attention away from yourself
senses.definitionCN: 把批评或注意力从自己身上引开
senses.example: He deflected the question with a joke.
senses.exampleCN: 他用一个玩笑把问题挡了回去。
senses.why: A thrown stone sent toward another wall.
senses.whyCN: 一块扔来的石头被引向另一堵墙。

intro.en: Deflect comes from Latin deflectere, to bend away, from de- plus flectere, to bend.
intro.cn: deflect 源自拉丁语 deflectere（弯开），由 de- 加 flectere（弯曲）构成。

items.en: Flectere meant to bend.
items.cn: flectere 意为弯曲。

items.en: Deflectere meant to bend away or turn aside.
items.cn: deflectere 意为弯开或转向一边。

items.en: Deflect entered English for turning a ray aside.
items.cn: 十七世纪 deflect 以使光线偏转义进入英语。

items.en: Deflect was used in physics and navigation.
items.cn: 十八世纪 deflect 用于物理与航海。

items.en: Deflect widened to weapons and sport.
items.cn: 十九世纪 deflect 扩展到武器与体育。

items.en: Deflect gained the sense of avoiding blame.
items.cn: 二十世纪 deflect 带上推卸责任的含义。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the flect- bending family; the near-meaning group names turning aside.
note.cn: 形近组共享 flect-（弯曲）家族；近义组都是「转向一边」的说法。
